+"""FastAPI router exposing the Living Studio sidecar API under ``/api``."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from fastapi import APIRouter, Query
+from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
+
+from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.chat import stream_chat
+from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.mcp_data import call_mcp_tool, fetch_canvas
+from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.probes import check_llm_health, defaults, is_endpoint_reachable
+from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.schemas import (
+    AddOutcomeRequest,
+    AddStepRequest,
+    ChatRequest,
+    LlmHealthRequest,
+    McpHealthRequest,
+)
+
+router = APIRouter(prefix="/api")
+
+
+@router.get("/config")
+def get_config() -> dict:
+    return {"defaults": defaults()}
+
+
+@router.post("/health/mcp")
+def post_mcp_health(body: McpHealthRequest) -> dict:
+    return {"reachable": is_endpoint_reachable(body.mcp_url)}
+
+
+@router.post("/health/llm")
+async def post_llm_health(body: LlmHealthRequest) -> dict:
+    healthy, message = await check_llm_health(body.base_url, body.api_key, body.model)
+    return {"healthy": healthy, "message": message}
+
+
+@router.get("/canvas")
+async def get_canvas(mcp_url: str = Query(...)) -> dict:
+    return await fetch_canvas(mcp_url)
+
+
+@router.post("/steps")
+async def post_step(body: AddStepRequest) -> dict:
+    result = await call_mcp_tool(
+        body.mcp_url,
+        "add_step",
+        {"job_id": body.job_id, "name": body.name, "order": body.order},
+    )
+    return {"ok": True, "result": result}
+
+
+@router.post("/outcomes")
+async def post_outcome(body: AddOutcomeRequest) -> dict:
+    result = await call_mcp_tool(
+        body.mcp_url,
+        "add_outcome",
+        {
+            "job_id": body.job_id,
+            "statement": body.statement,
+            "importance": body.importance,
+            "satisfaction": body.satisfaction,
+        },
+    )
+    return {"ok": True, "result": result}
+
+
+@router.post("/chat")
+async def post_chat(body: ChatRequest) -> StreamingResponse:
+    return StreamingResponse(
+        stream_chat(body),
+        media_type="text/event-stream",
+        headers={"Cache-Control": "no-cache", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"},
+    )

+    return f"http://127.0.0.1:{_closed_port()}{path}"
+

+class _ListeningSocket:
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
+        self._sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+        self._sock.listen(1)
+        self.port: int = self._sock.getsockname()[1]
+
+    def url(self, path: str = "/mcp") -> str:
+        return f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.port}{path}"
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self._sock.close()

+def _sse_events(body: str) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
+    events: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+    for block in body.split("\n\n"):
+        name = None
+        data = None
+        for line in block.splitlines():
+            if line.startswith("event: "):
+                name = line[len("event: ") :]
+            elif line.startswith("data: "):
+                data = line[len("data: ") :]
+        if name and data is not None:
+            events.setdefault(name, []).append(data)
+    return events
+

+def _chat_body(user_input: str, messages: list[dict[str, str]] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    history = list(messages or [])
+    history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_input})
+    return {**OFFLINE, "messages": history}

+    with _client().stream("POST", path, json=payload) as response:

+"""Branch tests for the streaming tool loop in ``studio.chat``."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import json
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from typing import Any
+
+from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio import chat
+from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.schemas import ChatMessage, ChatRequest
+
+
+def _request() -> ChatRequest:
+    return ChatRequest(
+        base_url="http://llm/v1",
+        api_key="key",
+        model="model",
+        mcp_url="http://mcp",
+        messages=[ChatMessage(role="user", content="list jobs")],
+    )
+
+
+class _FakeStream:
+    def __init__(self, chunks: list[Any]) -> None:
+        self._chunks = chunks
+
+    def __aiter__(self) -> Any:
+        async def _gen() -> Any:
+            for chunk in self._chunks:
+                yield chunk
+
+        return _gen()
+
+
+class _Completions:
+    def __init__(self, streams: list[_FakeStream]) -> None:
+        self._streams = streams
+
+    async def create(self, **kwargs: Any) -> _FakeStream:
+        return self._streams.pop(0)
+
+
+class _FakeOpenAI:
+    def __init__(self, streams: list[_FakeStream], **kwargs: Any) -> None:
+        self.chat = SimpleNamespace(completions=_Completions(streams))
+
+
+class _Mcp:
+    error: Exception | None = None
+    calls: list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]] = []
+
+    def __init__(self, url: str) -> None:
+        self.url = url
+
+    async def __aenter__(self) -> _Mcp:
+        return self
+
+    async def __aexit__(self, *exc: Any) -> bool:
+        return False
+
+    async def list_tools(self) -> list[Any]:
+        return [
+            SimpleNamespace(
+                name="get_jobs",
+                description="List jobs",
+                input_schema={"type": "object", "properties": {}},
+            )
+        ]
+
+    async def call_tool(self, name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+        self.calls.append((name, arguments))
+        if self.error is not None:
+            raise self.error
+        return "ok"
+
+
+def _chunk(content: str | None = None, tool_calls: list[Any] | None = None) -> Any:
+    delta = SimpleNamespace(content=content, tool_calls=tool_calls)
+    return SimpleNamespace(choices=[SimpleNamespace(delta=delta)])
+
+
+def _collect(request: ChatRequest) -> list[str]:
+    async def _run() -> list[str]:
+        return [chunk async for chunk in chat.stream_chat(request)]
+
+    return asyncio.run(_run())
+
+
+def _events(frames: list[str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
+    events: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+    for frame in frames:
+        name = None
+        data = None
+        for line in frame.splitlines():
+            if line.startswith("event: "):
+                name = line[len("event: ") :]
+            elif line.startswith("data: "):
+                data = line[len("data: ") :]
+        if name and data is not None:
+            events.setdefault(name, []).append(data)
+    return events
+
+
+def _install(monkeypatch, streams: list[_FakeStream]) -> None:
+    async def _healthy(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> tuple[bool, str]:
+        return True, "ok"
+
+    _Mcp.calls = []
+    _Mcp.error = None
+    monkeypatch.setattr(chat, "check_llm_health", _healthy)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(chat, "McpClient", _Mcp)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(chat, "AsyncOpenAI", lambda **kwargs: _FakeOpenAI(streams, **kwargs))
+
+
+def _tool_call(arguments: str) -> Any:
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        index=0,
+        id="call-1",
+        function=SimpleNamespace(name="get_jobs", arguments=arguments),
+    )
+
+
+def test_stream_chat_falls_back_to_empty_arguments_for_invalid_json(monkeypatch) -> None:
+    _install(
+        monkeypatch,
+        [
+            _FakeStream([_chunk(tool_calls=[_tool_call("not json")])]),
+            _FakeStream([_chunk("done")]),
+        ],
+    )
+
+    events = _events(_collect(_request()))
+
+    assert _Mcp.calls == [("get_jobs", {})]
+    assert json.loads(events["tool"][1])["status"] == "ok"
+
+
+def test_stream_chat_reports_tool_call_failures(monkeypatch) -> None:
+    _install(
+        monkeypatch,
+        [
+            _FakeStream([_chunk(tool_calls=[_tool_call("{}")])]),
+            _FakeStream([_chunk("recovered")]),
+        ],
+    )
+    _Mcp.error = RuntimeError("tool exploded")
+
+    events = _events(_collect(_request()))
+
+    failure = json.loads(events["tool"][1])
+    assert failure["status"] == "error"
+    assert "tool exploded" in failure["preview"]

+def test_is_endpoint_reachable_defaults_the_host() -> None:
+    assert probes.is_endpoint_reachable("http://:1/mcp", timeout=0.05) is False
+
+
+def test_classify_llm_error_detects_connection_failures() -> None:
+    assert probes.classify_llm_error(RuntimeError("Connection refused"))[0] == "connection_error"
+    assert probes.classify_llm_error(RuntimeError("timed out"))[0] == "connection_error"
+
+
+def test_classify_llm_error_keeps_other_errors_generic() -> None:
+    assert probes.classify_llm_error(RuntimeError("bad request")) == ("error", "bad request")
+
+
+def test_check_llm_health_reports_offline_without_connecting(monkeypatch) -> None:
+    monkeypatch.setattr(probes, "is_endpoint_reachable", lambda url, timeout: False)
+
+    healthy, message = asyncio.run(probes.check_llm_health("http://llm", "key", "model"))
+
+    assert healthy is False
+    assert message == probes.OFFLINE_MESSAGE
+
+
+def test_check_llm_health_reports_success(monkeypatch) -> None:
+    class _Models:
+        async def list(self) -> list[Any]:
+            return []
+
+    class _FakeOpenAI:
+        def __init__(self, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
+            self.models = _Models()
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(probes, "is_endpoint_reachable", lambda url, timeout: True)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(probes, "AsyncOpenAI", _FakeOpenAI)
+
+    healthy, message = asyncio.run(probes.check_llm_health("http://llm", "key", "model"))
+
+    assert healthy is True
+    assert message == "LLM backend is reachable."
+
+
+def test_check_llm_health_reports_connection_errors(monkeypatch) -> None:
+    class _Models:
+        async def list(self) -> list[Any]:
+            raise RuntimeError("connection refused")
+
+    class _FakeOpenAI:
+        def __init__(self, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
+            self.models = _Models()
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(probes, "is_endpoint_reachable", lambda url, timeout: True)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(probes, "AsyncOpenAI", _FakeOpenAI)
+
+    healthy, message = asyncio.run(probes.check_llm_health("http://llm", "key", "model"))
+
+    assert healthy is False
+    assert message == "connection_error: connection refused"
+

-  a local ``python -m mcp_server`` process or a hosted endpoint.
-
-Commands resolve a backend once from the options stored on
-:mod:`cli.context`. Keeping the local and remote paths behind one interface
-means the same command works against either, and a future hosted backend only
-has to implement ``call``.

-run.py — Local dev launcher for Agentic ODI.
-
-Starts the FastMCP server (``python -m mcp_server``) and the Living Studio
-sidecar (``uvicorn local_server.app:create_app --factory``) concurrently, then
-prints the MCP and Studio URLs. Shutting down this script (Ctrl+C) terminates
-both processes.
-
-Usage:
-    python -m client.run
-"""
-
-from __future__ import annotations
-
-import os
-import signal
-import socket
-import subprocess  # nosec B404 - launches only fixed child commands (see B603 notes)
-import sys
-import time
-
-MCP_PORT = 8000
-STUDIO_PORT = 8100
-
-REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(
-    os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
-)
-SPA_DIST = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "studio", "dist")
-SPA_BUILD_HINT = "Frontend not built — run `npm --prefix studio run build` to serve the Studio UI."
-
-
-def is_port_in_use(port: int) -> bool:
-    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
-        return s.connect_ex(("localhost", port)) == 0
-
-
-def build_commands() -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
-    """Return the (mcp_server, sidecar) argv lists, both shell-free and fixed."""
-    mcp_command = [sys.executable, "-m", "mcp_server"]
-    sidecar_command = [
-        sys.executable,
-        "-m",
-        "uvicorn",
-        "local_server.app:create_app",
-        "--factory",
-        "--host",
-        "127.0.0.1",
-        "--port",
-        str(STUDIO_PORT),
-    ]
-    return mcp_command, sidecar_command
-
-
-def start_server() -> subprocess.Popen:
-    if is_port_in_use(MCP_PORT):
-        print(f"Error: Port {MCP_PORT} is already in use.")
-        print("Please stop any process running on this port and try again.")
-        sys.exit(1)
-
-    mcp_command, _ = build_commands()
-    print(f"Starting MCP server on http://localhost:{MCP_PORT}/mcp ...")
-    # Fixed command, no shell, no untrusted input.
-    return subprocess.Popen(mcp_command)  # nosec B603
-
-
-def start_studio() -> subprocess.Popen:
-    if is_port_in_use(STUDIO_PORT):
-        print(f"Warning: Port {STUDIO_PORT} is already in use. The sidecar may fail to start.")
-
-    _, sidecar_command = build_commands()
-    print(f"Starting Living Studio sidecar on http://localhost:{STUDIO_PORT} ...")
-    # Fixed command, no shell, no untrusted input.
-    return subprocess.Popen(sidecar_command)  # nosec B603
-
-
-def main() -> None:
-    server = None
-    studio = None
-
-    def shutdown(signum=None, frame=None):
-        print("\nShutting down...")
-        if studio:
-            studio.terminate()
-        if server:
-            server.terminate()
-
-        try:
-            if studio:
-                studio.wait(timeout=5)
-            if server:
-                server.wait(timeout=5)
-        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
-            if studio:
-                studio.kill()
-            if server:
-                server.kill()
-
-        print("✅ All processes stopped.")
-        sys.exit(0)
-
-    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, shutdown)
-    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, shutdown)
-
-    try:
-        server = start_server()
-        # Give the server a moment to bind its port before the sidecar connects
-        time.sleep(2)
-        studio = start_studio()
-
-        print("\nBoth processes are running.")
-        print(f"MCP Server   -> http://localhost:{MCP_PORT}/mcp")
-        print(f"Living Studio -> http://localhost:{STUDIO_PORT}")
-        if not os.path.isdir(SPA_DIST):
-            print(f"\n⚠️  {SPA_BUILD_HINT}")
-        print("\nPress Ctrl+C to stop both.\n")
-
-        # Wait for either process to exit unexpectedly
-        while True:
-            rc_server = server.poll()
-            rc_studio = studio.poll()
-
-            if rc_server is not None:
-                print(f"\nServer exited unexpectedly (code {rc_server}).")
-                break
-
-            if rc_studio is not None:
-                print(f"\nStudio sidecar exited unexpectedly (code {rc_studio}).")
-                break
-
-            time.sleep(1)
-
-    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
-        print(f"\nError: {e}")
-    finally:
-        shutdown()
-
-

-    main()

 # Bundled CLI Distribution & Self-Update Implementation Plan
 
 > **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
 
 **Goal:** Ship `odi` as a self-contained per-platform binary installed via `curl … | sh`, with background auto-update and an explicit `odi update`, driven by an automated tag/release pipeline.
 
 **Architecture:** PyInstaller `--onedir` bundles the CLI plus its interpreter and dependency tree into a versioned directory; a small updater module downloads and atomically swaps a `current` symlink to a new version. release-please tags releases and a GitHub Actions matrix builds/attaches the archives.
 
 **Tech Stack:** Python 3.10+, Typer, pydantic v2, fastmcp, PyInstaller, uv, GitHub Actions, release-please.
 
 **Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-cli-bundled-distribution-design.md`
 
 ## Global Constraints
 
 - Python `>= 3.10` (workspace `requires-python`); CLI package `agentic-odi-cli`, entry `cli.cli:app`.
 - Binary/primary command name `odi`; aliases `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and legacy `agentic-odi`.
 - Versioning: **semver primary, release datetime secondary**. Tag `v<semver>`; embed `VERSION` and `RELEASE_DATE_UTC`.
 - First released version is **`0.1.0`**.
 - Install layout under `~/.local/share/agentic-odi/` (`versions/<v>`, `current` symlink); config/state under `~/.config/agentic-odi/`; bin dir `~/.local/bin`. All overridable via XDG env vars; install root also via `AGENTIC_ODI_INSTALL_DIR`.
 - **User-local install only** — the installer never escalates; no `/usr/local`, no sudo.
 - Auto-update is **on by default**, applies on next run, at most one check per 24h.
 - Update opt-outs: `--no-update` flag and env `AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE=1`. Auto-update is disabled for non-frozen (source) runs and non-writable install dirs.
 - Linux artifacts target **glibc 2.17-class** (build in a manylinux2014 / Ubuntu 20.04 container).
 - **No UPX. No code signing** (v1). Bundle full functionality so `--backend mcp` works.
 - Artifact names: `odi_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz` (unix) / `odi_<version>_<os>_<arch>.zip` (windows). `os`/`arch` ∈ {`linux`,`macos`,`windows`} × {`x86_64`,`arm64`}. A `checksums.txt` (SHA-256) ships alongside.
 - `local` backend is the CLI default; `mcp` preserves prior behavior (env `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL`, default `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
 - Repo `alehar9320/agentic-odi`; releases from GitHub Releases.
 
 ## Review Focus
 
 Uncovered inputs/conditions most likely to bite a user — each has a test in the task that owns the code:
 
 1. **Offline / network failure during update** — the command still runs; update silently no-ops. (Task 5)
 2. **Checksum mismatch / truncated download** — install is never corrupted; update aborts. (Task 4)
 3. **Interrupted swap** — `current` always points at a complete version dir; no partial state. (Task 4)
 4. **Non-writable install dir** — auto-update disables gracefully instead of erroring. (Task 5)
 5. **`odi update` on a source (non-frozen) install** — clear message, no crash, non-zero-free. (Task 6)
 6. **Concurrent invocations** — only one update proceeds; the other skips. (Task 4)
 7. **Local backend DB path** — directory is created on first write. (Task 3)

 # CLI ODI Entity Parity & Shared Store Implementation Plan
 
 > **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
 
 **Goal:** Give the `agentic-odi` CLI full create/read/update/delete access to every ODI entity (Job, Step, Desired Outcome, Customer Outcome incl. `value_metrics`), matching the MCP tool surface, backed by one persistent SQLite store shared by the CLI and the MCP server.
 
 **Architecture:** Extend the `core` repository/service layers with CRUD + cascade delete + FK validation for `Job`/`Step`/`Outcome`. Make `SQLiteRepository` read-through (replays new events before reads) so concurrent processes converge. Add a `build_repository()` factory. The MCP server selects that factory instead of `InMemoryRepository`. The CLI gains a global `--backend/--db/--mcp-url` resolved through a shared `Backend` abstraction, plus new command groups whose names reserve `outcomes` for the desired-outcome entity.
 
 **Tech Stack:** Python 3.10+, Typer, Pydantic v2, FastMCP, SQLite (`IntentStore` append-only event log, WAL), pytest/pytest-asyncio, ruff, mypy.
 
 **Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-cli-odi-entity-parity-design.md`
 
 ## Global Constraints
 
 - Python `>=3.10`; every project targets `py310`, ruff line-length 100.
 - Ruff select: `["E4", "E7", "E9", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "BLE"]`.
 - Opportunity Score formula: `importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)` — reuse `compute_opportunity_score`.
 - `importance`/`satisfaction` valid range is `1.0`–`10.0`.
 - Store path env var: `AGENTIC_ODI_DB`; default `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`; value `:memory:` means in-memory.
 - CLI backend env var: `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND`; default `local`.
 - Command vocabulary: `jobs`, `steps`, `outcomes` (Desired Outcome), `customer-outcomes` (Customer Outcome), top-level `score`.
 - No CLI alias preserving the old `outcomes` = Customer Outcome meaning.
 - Deleting a Job cascades to its Steps, Outcomes, Customer Outcomes; deleting a Step cascades to Outcomes/Customer Outcomes bound to it. Creating a Step/Outcome/Customer Outcome under an unknown `job_id`/`step_id` is rejected.
 - Updates use the `is not None` sentinel convention: a field is never cleared by passing null; `job_id` is immutable.
 - Tests must never touch the real `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`.
 - Run all tests via `uv run --directory <pkg> pytest`; lint/type via the README commands.
 
 ## Review Focus
 
 These are the failure modes most likely to bite a user; each has its test pinned in the owning task.
 
 1. **Concurrent writer visibility** — a CLI `local` write while the MCP server is running must be visible to the server's next read (Task 3, 5).
 2. **Cascade delete replay** — deleting a Job then restarting must not resurrect its dependents; a cascaded id reads as not-found (Task 1, 3).
 3. **Stored opportunity score on update** — updating only `importance` recomputes `opportunity_score`; clearing either score sets it to `None` (Task 2, 3).
 4. **Bad CLI inputs** — unknown `--backend`, `--db` combined with `--backend mcp`, malformed `--value-metric` JSON, and out-of-range scores produce a clear error, never a traceback (Task 6, 7, 8, 9, 10).
 5. **value_metrics semantics** — out-of-range or missing required metric fields are rejected; on update, supplying `--value-metric` replaces the whole list (Task 5, 10).

Missing env or HTTP/network error ⇒ raise `RuntimeError` (main exits 1).
   - `validate.validate_notes(notes: ReleaseNotes, manifest: dict) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]` — returns `(violations, warnings)`:
     - **G2** every cited source resolves: `len(cited) >= 7` and some manifest `sha.startswith(cited)` ⇒ else `f"G2: cited sha not in release range: {cited}"`.
     - **G3/G7** enforced by the pydantic models (min lengths, non-empty sections) + one check: total entries ≥ 1 ⇒ else `"G3: changelog has no entries"`.
     - **G4** every commit with `core.convention.is_coverage_required` cited ⇒ else `f"G4: uncovered {type} commit {sha[:7]} {subject}"`.
     - **G6a** hard risky tokens in entry text not present in manifest text (concat of subject+body+files): backtick spans `` `…` ``, `snake_case` tokens (`\b[a-z0-9]+_[a-z0-9_]+\b`), file paths with extension (`\b[\w.-]+/[\w./-]+\.\w+\b`), `x.y.z` versions (`\b\d+\.\d+\.\d+\b`) ⇒ `f"G6a: ungrounded token in entry: {tok}"`.

Returns 1 for usage/git/env/model errors (message to stderr, no traceback).

 # Input
 You receive one JSON manifest: every commit in this release (full SHA, subject, body, parsed type/scope/breaking, changed files). It is the only information you may use.

 2. Write plain-language, value-focused sentences: one sentence per entry, ideally under 200 characters. Never quote commit subjects verbatim; no scopes, branch names, PR numbers, jargon, exclamation marks, or emoji.
 3. Group entries under exactly these section names and omit empty ones: "Initial release" (only when manifest.initial is true), "Added", "Improved", "Fixed", "Security", "Removed". Keep this order.
 4. Every entry cites the full 40-character SHA of at least one manifest commit in "sources".
 5. Every manifest commit with type feat, fix, perf, or revert, or marked breaking, MUST be covered by at least one entry. Do not invent entries that cite nothing.
 6. Do not create entries for chore, ci, build, test, docs, style, or dependency-bump commits unless the commit clearly describes a user benefit. Put refactor commits under "Improved" only when the commit states a user-visible benefit.
 7. Set "breaking": true for entries summarizing a breaking commit and start that entry's text with "Breaking change: ".

@@ -0,0 +1,178 @@
+# Repository Structure Design
+
+**Date:** 2026-10-20
+
+**Status:** Approved
+
+## Intent
+
+Make the repository legible to humans and agents by naming folders after their
+functional role, making the dependency direction explicit, and removing
+accidental packaging and persistence divergence.
+
+The repository is a Python uv workspace plus a React/Tauri frontend. It currently
+has six Python distributions, a frontend, deployment assets, release tooling, and
+several agent harness directories at the root. The folder names describe
+technology (`core`, `client`, `local_server`) rather than responsibility, so a
+new contributor cannot tell what is deployable, what is a library, or who owns
+persistence.
+
+## Goals
+
+- Separate deployable applications (`apps/`) from importable libraries
+  (`packages/`), infrastructure (`infra/`), packaging, scripts, and docs.
+- Give every folder a one-line functional responsibility in
+  `docs/architecture/README.md`.
+- Replace generic import roots (`core`, `cli`, `client`, `connectors`) with
+  unambiguous `agentic_odi_*` package names.
+- Remove the dev-only `client` distribution; keep the launcher as
+  `scripts/dev.py`.
+- Consolidate ruff, mypy, pytest, coverage, and bandit configuration at the
+  workspace root; keep only package-specific deltas in package `pyproject.toml`
+  files.
+- Make the MCP tool contract a single source of truth in core, enforced by a
+  cross-package contract test.
+- Make SQLite the default persistence for every runtime, with in-memory
+  repositories reserved for tests.
+- Remove stale repository copies, generated artifacts, and misleading agent
+  instructions from the working tree.
+
+## Non-Goals
+
+- No behavioral redesign of the ODI domain model or scoring algorithm.
+- No change to the MCP transport (HTTP) or tool semantics.
+- No new features in the Studio SPA or Tauri shell.
+- No independent release cadence per package. The workspace remains
+  single-versioned.
+- No rewrite of the CLI command surface beyond import and entry-point updates.
+
+## Constraints
+
+- Python floor stays `>=3.10`; `connectors` must stop targeting 3.11.
+- Use the existing `src/` layout and hatchling build backend.
+- Keep tests co-located with each package. Root `tests/` holds cross-package
+  contract tests only.
+- Preserve git history with file moves where practical.
+- `/studio` remains a single frontend project containing the Tauri shell.
+- The release pipeline, PyInstaller spec, installers, Coverage/Codecov, and
+  GitHub workflows must keep working.
+- Existing uncommitted work in the tree must not be discarded.
+
+## Target Layout
+
+```text
+agentic-odi/
+├── apps/
+│   ├── cli/                    # agentic-odi-cli -> agentic_odi_cli
+│   ├── mcp-server/             # agentic-odi-mcp-server -> agentic_odi_mcp_server
+│   ├── studio-api/             # ex-local_server -> agentic_odi_studio_api
+│   └── studio/                 # React/Vite SPA + src-tauri
+├── packages/
+│   ├── core/                   # agentic-odi-core -> agentic_odi_core
+│   └── connectors/             # agentic-odi-connectors -> agentic_odi_connectors
+├── infra/cloudflare/           # worker.ts + deployment adapter
+├── packaging/pyinstaller/
+├── scripts/                    # dev.py, build_binary.sh, installers, tests
+├── tests/contract/             # cross-package MCP contract tests
+├── docs/
+│   ├── architecture/           # repo map, data flow, testing
+│   ├── reference/              # ODI source-of-truth material
+│   └── superpowers/            # specs and plans
+├── pyproject.toml              # workspace + shared tooling
+├── uv.lock
+├── README.md
+├── AGENTS.md
+└── CHANGELOG.md
+```
+
+## Decisions
+
+### Five Python projects, not six
+
+`client` is a development-only process launcher. It has no runtime consumers and
+does not justify a distribution, a test suite entry, or a CI step. It becomes
+`scripts/dev.py`.
+
+The remaining five distributions stay separate because they have materially
+different dependencies and artifacts: the CLI is shipped as a PyInstaller
+binary, the MCP server is a protocol adapter, and the Studio API is a FastAPI
+sidecar. Consolidating them can be revisited later without changing the folder
+roles.
+
+### Import names are versioned by project, not split by namespace
+
+Each distribution uses a distinct top-level import package
+(`agentic_odi_core`, `agentic_odi_cli`, etc.) rather than a split
+`agentic_odi.*` namespace. This keeps editable installs, PyInstaller hidden
+imports, and test imports unambiguous.
+
+### Core owns the MCP contract
+
+Core exposes `contract.py` with tool names and argument models. The MCP server,
+CLI backend, and Studio API consume those names instead of duplicating string
+literals. A root contract test asserts that the live FastMCP tool registry
+matches the contract.
+
+### SQLite is the default persistence for every runtime
+
+The MCP server, CLI, and Studio API instantiate `ODIService` with
+`SQLiteRepository` by default. `InMemoryRepository` is test-only. This removes
+the current situation where `agentic-odi` local data and data served over MCP
+can differ.
+
+### Studio API uses the local service for data, MCP for chat
+
+In local mode, Studio data endpoints read and write through `ODIService` rather
+than making an HTTP round trip to the MCP server. The conversational tool loop
+continues to use MCP because that is the protocol being exercised. A backend
+selector mirrors the CLI's `local|mcp` option.
+
+### Asset paths are configured, not inferred from package depth
+
+The Studio API and dev launcher resolve the SPA directory from
+`AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DIST` with a development fallback. They no longer depend on
+`parents[3]`, which breaks on every move.
+
+## Migration Phases
+
+1. **Hygiene:** remove the stale `origin/` copy, ignore local worktrees and
+   harness state, remove generated artifacts, relocate the ODI reference PDF,
+   and fix stale Streamlit instructions.
+2. **Tooling:** move shared ruff/mypy/pytest/coverage/bandit config to the root,
+   standardize Python 3.10, collapse CI commands.
+3. **Python layout:** move core, connectors, cli, mcp_server, and local_server;
+   rename import packages and distribution names; update workspace members,
+   entry points, PyInstaller, build scripts, CI, and docs.
+4. **Launcher:** move the client launcher to `scripts/dev.py` and delete the
+   `client` distribution.
+5. **Frontend/infra:** move `studio/` to `apps/studio/`, `cloudflare/` to
+   `infra/cloudflare/`, and update Vite, Tauri, Wrangler, and release paths.
+6. **Contract/persistence:** add the core contract, contract tests, SQLite
+   defaults for MCP, Studio API local data path, and architecture docs.
+
+## Verification
+
+Each phase ends with the applicable subset of:
+
+```bash
+uv run ruff check .
+uv run ruff format --check .
+uv run mypy apps packages
+uv run pytest
+uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages
+npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck
+npm --prefix apps/studio run test
+npm --prefix apps/studio run build
+bash scripts/build_binary.sh   # VERSION set
+```
+
+## Risks
+
+- Import renames touch nearly every test; do the sweep with ripgrep and run the
+  full suite before moving on.
+- PyInstaller hidden imports and `_build_info.py` paths must be updated with the
+  CLI move.
+- Tauri and Wrangler configs contain relative asset paths; verify both the web
+  build and the desktop config parsing after the frontend move.
+- Release workflows reference `scripts/`, `packaging/`, and `cli/src`; update
+  them in the same phase as the move.

-def is_endpoint_reachable(url: str, timeout: float = 0.3) -> bool:
-    """Quick socket check to verify a port is open without hanging on HTTP reads."""

-        "failed to establish a new connection",
-        "timed out",
-        "timeout",
-        "connection refused",
-    ]

+"""Ready-to-use MCP connector presets for common ODI workflows.
+
+Each preset captures everything needed to register a connector for a well-known
+MCP server: the endpoint, how it authenticates, and where its documentation
+lives. Presets are grouped by the five capability areas an outcome-driven
+innovation process needs, so a new workspace can be wired up with
+``agentic-odi connectors add mcp --preset <id>`` instead of hunting for URLs.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from typing import Any, Literal
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import ConnectorConfig
+
+CapabilityArea = Literal[
+    "voice-of-customer",
+    "quantitative-data",
+    "market-intelligence",
+    "strategy-alignment",
+    "knowledge-output",
+]
+
+AREA_LABELS: dict[CapabilityArea, str] = {
+    "voice-of-customer": "Voice of customer & qualitative research",
+    "quantitative-data": "Quantitative data & opportunity scoring",
+    "market-intelligence": "Market & competitive intelligence",
+    "strategy-alignment": "Product strategy & backlog alignment",
+    "knowledge-output": "Strategy & knowledge management output",
+}
+
+ENV_VAR_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}")
+
+
+class UnknownPresetError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, preset_id: str) -> None:
+        self.preset_id = preset_id
+        super().__init__(f"Unknown preset: {preset_id} (try 'agentic-odi connectors catalog')")
+
+
+class UnknownAreaError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, area: str) -> None:
+        self.area = area
+        valid = ", ".join(AREA_LABELS)
+        super().__init__(f"Unknown capability area: {area} (expected one of: {valid})")
+
+
+class ConnectorPreset(BaseModel):
+    """A known MCP server plus the credentials it needs."""
+
+    id: str
+    label: str
+    area: CapabilityArea
+    summary: str
+    url: str
+    auth: Literal["none", "oauth"] = "none"
+    env_vars: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    headers: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+    docs: str
+    tools: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+
+    def referenced_env_vars(self) -> set[str]:
+        """Environment variables the URL or headers interpolate with ``${VAR}``."""
+        found: set[str] = set()
+        for value in [self.url, *self.headers.values()]:
+            found.update(ENV_VAR_PATTERN.findall(value))
+        return found
+
+
+PRESETS: tuple[ConnectorPreset, ...] = (
+    # 1. Voice of customer & qualitative research
+    ConnectorPreset(
+        id="notion",
+        label="Notion",
+        area="voice-of-customer",
+        summary="Interview notes, feedback logs, and PRDs from Notion pages.",
+        url="https://mcp.notion.com/mcp",
+        auth="oauth",
+        docs="https://developers.notion.com/docs/mcp",
+    ),
+    ConnectorPreset(
+        id="gong",
+        label="Gong",
+        area="voice-of-customer",
+        summary="Sales and success call transcripts with direct customer quotes.",
+        url="https://mcp.gong.io/mcp",
+        auth="oauth",

+"""Kind registry that maps connector configs onto Connector implementations."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Callable
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.mcp.connector import MCPClientConnector
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import ConnectorConfig, McpConnectorSettings
+from agentic_odi_connectors.protocol import Connector
+from agentic_odi_connectors.registry import UnknownConnectorKindError
+
+Builder = Callable[[ConnectorConfig], Connector]
+
+_builders: dict[str, Builder] = {}
+
+
+def register_kind(kind: str, builder: Builder) -> None:
+    """Register a builder for a connector kind (mcp today; others later)."""
+    _builders[kind] = builder
+
+
+def known_kinds() -> set[str]:
+    return set(_builders)
+
+
+def build_connector(config: ConnectorConfig) -> Connector:
+    try:
+        builder = _builders[config.kind]
+    except KeyError:
+        raise UnknownConnectorKindError(config.kind) from None
+    return builder(config)
+
+
+def _build_mcp(config: ConnectorConfig) -> Connector:
+    settings = McpConnectorSettings.model_validate(config.settings)
+    return MCPClientConnector(name=config.name, settings=settings)
+
+
+register_kind("mcp", _build_mcp)

@@ -0,0 +1,176 @@
+"""MCP client connector that ingests tools and resources from an external server."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import os
+import re
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from typing import Any
+
+from fastmcp import Client, FastMCP
+from fastmcp.client.transports import StreamableHttpTransport
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import (
+    HealthStatus,
+    IngestBatch,
+    IngestRecord,
+    McpConnectorSettings,
+)
+from agentic_odi_connectors.protocol import Connector
+
+_ENV_VAR_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}")
+
+
+class MissingEnvironmentError(RuntimeError):
+    """Raised when a connector needs credentials that are not in the environment."""
+
+    def __init__(self, names: list[str]) -> None:
+        self.names = names
+        super().__init__("Missing environment variable(s): " + ", ".join(names))
+
+
+def _expand_env(value: str, environ: Mapping[str, str]) -> str:
+    return _ENV_VAR_PATTERN.sub(lambda match: environ.get(match.group(1), ""), value)
+
+
+def _to_dict(obj: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    if hasattr(obj, "model_dump"):
+        dumped = obj.model_dump(mode="json")
+        if isinstance(dumped, dict):
+            return dumped
+    return {"repr": repr(obj)}
+
+
+def _content_text(obj: Any) -> str:
+    parts: list[str] = []
+    content = getattr(obj, "content", None)
+    if content is None:
+        text = getattr(obj, "text", None)
+        return text if isinstance(text, str) else json.dumps(_to_dict(obj))
+    for item in content:
+        text = getattr(item, "text", None)
+        if isinstance(text, str):
+            parts.append(text)
+    return "\n".join(parts) if parts else json.dumps(_to_dict(obj))
+
+
+class MCPClientConnector(Connector):
+    """Pulls catalog, resources, and optional tool results from an MCP server."""
+
+    kind = "mcp"
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        name: str,
+        settings: McpConnectorSettings,
+        *,
+        server: FastMCP | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.name = name
+        self.settings = settings
+        self._server = server
+
+    def transport(self) -> StreamableHttpTransport | FastMCP:
+        """Build the MCP transport, resolving credentials from the environment."""
+        if self._server is not None:
+            return self._server
+        missing = sorted(name for name in self.settings.env_vars if not os.environ.get(name))
+        if missing:
+            raise MissingEnvironmentError(missing)
+        headers = {
+            key: _expand_env(value, os.environ) for key, value in self.settings.headers.items()
+        }
+        return StreamableHttpTransport(
+            url=_expand_env(self.settings.url, os.environ),
+            headers=headers or None,
+            auth="oauth" if self.settings.auth == "oauth" else None,
+        )
+
+    def _client(self) -> Client:
+        return Client(self.transport())
+
+    async def health(self) -> HealthStatus:
+        try:
+            async with self._client() as client:
+                tools = await client.list_tools()
+                resources = await client.list_resources()
+            return HealthStatus(
+                ok=True,
+                message="reachable",
+                details={
+                    "tool_count": len(tools),
+                    "resource_count": len(resources),
+                },
+            )
+        except MissingEnvironmentError as exc:
+            return HealthStatus(
+                ok=False,
+                message=str(exc),
+                details={"missing_env": exc.names},
+            )
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            return HealthStatus(ok=False, message=str(exc))
+
+    async def ingest(self) -> IngestBatch:
+        batch = IngestBatch(connector_name=self.name)
+        try:
+            async with self._client() as client:
+                tools = await client.list_tools()
+                resources = await client.list_resources()
+                tool_dicts = [_to_dict(tool) for tool in tools]
+                resource_dicts = [_to_dict(resource) for resource in resources]
+                catalog_raw = {"tools": tool_dicts, "resources": resource_dicts}
+                batch.records.append(
+                    IngestRecord(
+                        source_name=self.name,
+                        source_kind=self.kind,
+                        item_type="catalog",
+                        name="mcp-catalog",
+                        content=json.dumps(catalog_raw, indent=2),
+                        raw=catalog_raw,
+                    )
+                )
+                for resource in resources:
+                    uri = str(getattr(resource, "uri", ""))
+                    name = str(getattr(resource, "name", None) or uri)
+                    try:
+                        contents = await client.read_resource(uri)
+                        content_text = "\n".join(
+                            getattr(item, "text", "") or "" for item in contents
+                        )
+                        batch.records.append(
+                            IngestRecord(
+                                source_name=self.name,
+                                source_kind=self.kind,
+                                item_type="resource",
+                                name=name,
+                                content=content_text,
+                                raw={"uri": uri, "resource": _to_dict(resource)},
+                            )
+                        )
+                    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+                        batch.errors.append(f"Failed to read resource {uri}: {exc}")
+                configured_tools = self.settings.tools
+                available = {str(getattr(tool, "name", "")) for tool in tools}
+                for tool_name in configured_tools:
+                    if tool_name not in available:
+                        batch.errors.append(f"Tool not found: {tool_name}")
+                        continue
+                    try:
+                        result = await client.call_tool(tool_name, {})
+                        batch.records.append(
+                            IngestRecord(
+                                source_name=self.name,
+                                source_kind=self.kind,
+                                item_type="tool_result",
+                                name=tool_name,
+                                content=_content_text(result),
+                                raw={"tool": tool_name, "result": _to_dict(result)},
+                            )
+                        )
+                    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+                        batch.errors.append(f"Failed to call tool {tool_name}: {exc}")
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            batch.errors.append(str(exc))
+        return batch

+"""Shared Pydantic models for external connectors and ingest records."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import uuid
+from typing import Any, Literal
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+ItemType = Literal["resource", "tool_result", "catalog"]
+McpAuthMode = Literal["none", "oauth"]
+
+
+class HealthStatus(BaseModel):
+    ok: bool
+    message: str
+    details: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+
+
+class IngestRecord(BaseModel):
+    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
+    source_name: str
+    source_kind: str
+    item_type: ItemType
+    name: str
+    content: str
+    raw: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+
+
+class IngestBatch(BaseModel):
+    connector_name: str
+    records: list[IngestRecord] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    errors: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+class McpConnectorSettings(BaseModel):
+    """Connection details for an MCP server.
+
+    ``url`` and ``headers`` may interpolate environment variables with
+    ``${VAR}`` so registry files never hold tokens. ``env_vars`` names the
+    variables that must be present before connecting.
+    """
+
+    url: str
+    tools: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    auth: McpAuthMode = "none"
+    headers: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+    env_vars: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+class ConnectorConfig(BaseModel):
+    name: str
+    kind: str
+    enabled: bool = True
+    settings: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

+"""JSON-backed registry of named connector configurations."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import ConnectorConfig
+
+
+class UnknownConnectorKindError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, kind: str) -> None:
+        self.kind = kind
+        super().__init__(f"Unknown connector kind: {kind}")
+
+
+class DuplicateConnectorError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
+        self.name = name
+        super().__init__(f"Connector already exists: {name}")
+
+
+class ConnectorNotFoundError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
+        self.name = name
+        super().__init__(f"Connector not found: {name}")
+
+
+def _known_kinds() -> set[str]:
+    from agentic_odi_connectors.factory import known_kinds
+
+    return known_kinds()
+
+
+class ConnectorRegistry:
+    """Persists connector configs to a JSON file."""
+
+    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
+        self.path = path
+
+    def add(self, config: ConnectorConfig) -> None:
+        if config.kind not in _known_kinds():
+            raise UnknownConnectorKindError(config.kind)
+        connectors = self._load()
+        if any(existing.name == config.name for existing in connectors):
+            raise DuplicateConnectorError(config.name)
+        connectors.append(config)
+        self._save(connectors)
+
+    def list_all(self) -> list[ConnectorConfig]:
+        return self._load()
+
+    def get(self, name: str) -> ConnectorConfig:
+        for config in self._load():
+            if config.name == name:
+                return config
+        raise ConnectorNotFoundError(name)
+
+    def _load(self) -> list[ConnectorConfig]:
+        if not self.path.exists():
+            return []
+        with self.path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            payload: dict[str, Any] = json.load(handle)
+        raw_connectors = payload.get("connectors", [])
+        return [ConnectorConfig.model_validate(item) for item in raw_connectors]
+
+    def _save(self, connectors: list[ConnectorConfig]) -> None:
+        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        payload = {"connectors": [item.model_dump(mode="json") for item in connectors]}
+        with self.path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            json.dump(payload, handle, indent=2)
+            handle.write("\n")

+"""In-memory ingest sink owned by the connectors package."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from agentic_odi_connectors.models import IngestBatch, IngestRecord
+
+
+class IngestSink:
+    """Stores ingested batches for the current process."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._batches: list[IngestBatch] = []
+
+    def append(self, batch: IngestBatch) -> None:
+        self._batches.append(batch)
+
+    def batches(self) -> list[IngestBatch]:
+        return list(self._batches)
+
+    def records(self) -> list[IngestRecord]:
+        return [record for batch in self._batches for record in batch.records]
+
+    def clear(self) -> None:
+        self._batches.clear()
+
+
+_default_sink = IngestSink()
+
+
+def get_default_sink() -> IngestSink:
+    return _default_sink

+from __future__ import annotations

+def test_preset_ids_are_unique() -> None:
+    ids = [preset.id for preset in PRESETS]
+
+    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids))

+def test_every_capability_area_is_covered() -> None:
+    assert {preset.area for preset in PRESETS} == set(AREA_LABELS)

+def test_presets_use_https_endpoints_and_docs() -> None:
+    for preset in PRESETS:

+        assert preset.docs.startswith("https://"), preset.id
+        assert preset.summary, preset.id
+
+
+def test_interpolated_env_vars_are_declared() -> None:
+    for preset in PRESETS:
+        referenced = set(ENV_REF.findall(preset.url))
+        for value in preset.headers.values():
+            referenced |= set(ENV_REF.findall(value))

+        assert referenced <= set(preset.env_vars), preset.id

+"""Single source of truth for the MCP tool surface.
+
+Adapters must use :class:`ToolName` instead of hard-coded strings, and the
+contract test in ``tests/contract`` asserts that the live FastMCP registry
+matches :data:`TOOL_SPECS`.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from enum import Enum
+
+
+class ToolName(str, Enum):
+    ADD_JOB = "add_job"
+    GET_JOBS = "get_jobs"
+    GET_JOB = "get_job"
+    ADD_STEP = "add_step"
+    GET_JOB_MAP = "get_job_map"
+    ADD_OUTCOME = "add_outcome"
+    GET_OUTCOMES = "get_outcomes"
+    ADD_CUSTOMER_OUTCOME = "add_customer_outcome"

+    COMPUTE_OPPORTUNITY = "compute_opportunity"
+    GET_FRAMEWORK_GUIDELINES = "get_odi_framework_guidelines"
+    GET_CAPABILITIES = "get_capabilities"
+    GREET = "greet"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ToolSpec:
+    """Argument names exposed by a tool and the subset that is required."""
+
+    arguments: tuple[str, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)
+    required: tuple[str, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)
+
+
+TOOL_SPECS: dict[str, ToolSpec] = {
+    ToolName.ADD_JOB.value: ToolSpec(("name", "description"), ("name",)),
+    ToolName.GET_JOBS.value: ToolSpec(),
+    ToolName.GET_JOB.value: ToolSpec(("job_id",), ("job_id",)),
+    ToolName.ADD_STEP.value: ToolSpec(("job_id", "name", "order"), ("job_id", "name", "order")),
+    ToolName.GET_JOB_MAP.value: ToolSpec(("job_id",), ("job_id",)),
+    ToolName.ADD_OUTCOME.value: ToolSpec(

+        ("job_id", "statement"),
+    ),
+    ToolName.GET_OUTCOMES.value: ToolSpec(("job_id", "step_id"), ("job_id",)),
+    ToolName.ADD_CUSTOMER_OUTCOME.value: ToolSpec(
+        ("job_id", "customer_value", "business_value", "step_id"),
+        ("job_id", "customer_value", "business_value"),
+    ),
+    ToolName.GET_CUSTOMER_OUTCOME.value: ToolSpec(("outcome_id",), ("outcome_id",)),
+    ToolName.LIST_CUSTOMER_OUTCOMES.value: ToolSpec(("job_id",)),
+    ToolName.UPDATE_CUSTOMER_OUTCOME.value: ToolSpec(
+        (
+            "outcome_id",
+            "direction",
+            "unit_of_measure",
+            "object_of_control",
+            "contextual_clarifier",
+            "statement",
+            "importance",
+            "satisfaction",
+            "category",
+            "business_statement",
+            "detail",
+            "estimated_annual_value",
+            "confidence",
+            "step_id",
+        ),
+        ("outcome_id",),
+    ),
+    ToolName.DELETE_CUSTOMER_OUTCOME.value: ToolSpec(("outcome_id",), ("outcome_id",)),
+    ToolName.COMPUTE_OPPORTUNITY.value: ToolSpec(
+        ("importance", "satisfaction"), ("importance", "satisfaction")
+    ),
+    ToolName.GET_FRAMEWORK_GUIDELINES.value: ToolSpec(),
+    ToolName.GET_CAPABILITIES.value: ToolSpec(),
+    ToolName.GREET.value: ToolSpec(("name",), ("name",)),
+}

+"""Append-only Intent Store (CTO specification)."""
+
+import json
+import sqlite3
+from datetime import datetime
+
+
+class IntentStore:
+    def __init__(self, db_path: str = "intent_store.db") -> None:
+        # Connect to SQLite in WAL mode for high-performance concurrency
+        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
+        self.conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;")
+        self._init_db()
+
+    def _init_db(self) -> None:
+        """Creates an immutable, append-only event table."""
+        with self.conn:
+            self.conn.execute(
+                """
+                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
+                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
+                    timestamp TEXT NOT NULL,
+                    event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
+                    payload TEXT NOT NULL
+                )
+            """
+            )
+
+    def append(self, event_type: str, payload: dict) -> None:
+        """Appends a new event to the stream (Immutable write)."""
+        timestamp = datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
+        payload_json = json.dumps(payload)
+        with self.conn:
+            self.conn.execute(
+                "INSERT INTO events (timestamp, event_type, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
+                (timestamp, event_type, payload_json),
+            )
+
+    def get_stream(self) -> list[dict]:
+        """Retrieves the full chronological event stream for AI reasoning."""
+        cursor = self.conn.cursor()
+        cursor.execute("SELECT id, timestamp, event_type, payload FROM events ORDER BY id ASC")
+        return [
+            {
+                "id": row[0],
+                "timestamp": row[1],
+                "type": row[2],
+                "payload": json.loads(row[3]) if row[3] else {},
+            }
+            for row in cursor.fetchall()
+        ]
+
+    def clear(self) -> None:
+        """Clear all events (for testing)."""
+        with self.conn:
+            self.conn.execute("DELETE FROM events")
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self.conn.close()

+ODI_ASSISTANT_PROMPT = """You are an expert in Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI). Your purpose is to help users discover, define, and prioritize high-value jobs, desired outcomes, and opportunities."""
+
+ODI_FRAMEWORK_GUIDELINES = """## Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) — Stage-by-Stage Tool Guide
+
+Follow this sequence when guiding a user through the ODI process:
+
+### Stage 1: Define Intent (Job-to-be-Done)
+- **When**: Always start here if no Job exists.
+- **Ask the user**: 'What is the main task or goal your customer is trying to accomplish?'
+- **Tools to use**:
+  - `add_job(name, description)` — Create the Job once identified.
+  - `get_jobs()` — Check if a relevant Job already exists before creating a new one.
+  - `get_job(job_id)` — Retrieve details of a specific existing Job.
+
+### Stage 2: Capture Desired Outcomes
+- **When**: After a Job is defined. Outcomes come BEFORE steps or solutions.
+- **Ask the user**: 'What does success look like? What should happen faster, more reliably, or more consistently?'
+- **Outcome statement format**: 'Minimize/Maximize the [metric] when [context].'
+- **Tools to use**:
+  - `add_outcome(job_id, statement, importance, satisfaction)` — Capture each desired outcome with scores.
+  - `get_outcomes(job_id)` — Review all outcomes captured for a Job.
+
+### Stage 3: Calculate Opportunity Scores
+- **When**: After outcomes have importance and satisfaction scores.
+- **Formula**: Opportunity Score = importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)
+- **Scores > 10** indicate high innovation opportunity. Guide the user to focus efforts there.
+- **Tools to use**: `get_outcomes(job_id)` — Review opportunity_score field on each outcome.
+
+### Stage 4: Build the Job Map
+- **When**: After key outcomes are captured. Use to organize the job execution context.
+- **Ask the user**: 'What are the key phases or steps the customer takes when doing this job?'
+- **Tools to use**:
+  - `add_step(job_id, name, order)` — Add each chronological step.
+  - `get_job_map(job_id)` — View the complete ordered job map.
+
+### General Rule
+Never skip stages. Always confirm the user has a Job defined (Stage 1) before capturing Outcomes (Stage 2), and always capture Outcomes (Stage 2) before building the Job Map (Stage 4)."""

+"""Core domain models for Agentic ODI."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import uuid
+from enum import Enum
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, computed_field
+
+
+class Direction(str, Enum):
+    MINIMIZE = "minimize"
+    MAXIMIZE = "maximize"
+
+
+class BusinessImpactCategory(str, Enum):
+    REVENUE_GROWTH = "revenue_growth"
+    COST_REDUCTION = "cost_reduction"
+    RETENTION = "retention"
+    RISK_MITIGATION = "risk_mitigation"
+    OPERATIONAL_EFFICIENCY = "operational_efficiency"
+    COMPLIANCE = "compliance"
+    BRAND_REPUTATION = "brand_reputation"
+    OTHER = "other"
+
+
+def compute_opportunity_score(importance: float, satisfaction: float) -> float:
+    """ODI Opportunity Score = importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)."""
+    return float(importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0.0))
+
+
+class Job(BaseModel):
+    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
+    name: str = Field(..., description="The name of the Job-to-be-Done")
+    description: str | None = Field(None, description="Detailed description of the Job")
+
+
+class Step(BaseModel):
+    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
+    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this step belongs to")
+    name: str = Field(..., description="The name of the job step")
+    order: int = Field(..., description="The chronological order of this step in the job map")
+
+
+class Outcome(BaseModel):
+    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
+    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this outcome relates to")
+    step_id: str | None = Field(None, description="The ID of the specific Step, if applicable")
+    statement: str = Field(
+        ..., description="The desired outcome statement (e.g., 'Minimize the time it takes to...')"
+    )
+    importance: float | None = Field(None, ge=1.0, le=10.0, description="Importance score (1-10)")
+    satisfaction: float | None = Field(
+        None, ge=1.0, le=10.0, description="Current satisfaction score (1-10)"
+    )
+    opportunity_score: float | None = Field(
+        None, description="Opportunity score (Importance + max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0))"
+    )
+
+
+class ValueMetric(BaseModel):
+    name: str
+    direction: Direction
+    unit_of_measure: str
+    importance: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
+    satisfaction: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
+
+    @computed_field
+    @property
+    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
+        return compute_opportunity_score(self.importance, self.satisfaction)
+
+
+class CustomerValue(BaseModel):
+    direction: Direction
+    unit_of_measure: str
+    object_of_control: str
+    contextual_clarifier: str | None = None
+    statement: str
+    importance: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
+    satisfaction: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
+    value_metrics: list[ValueMetric] = Field(default_factory=list)
+
+    @computed_field
+    @property
+    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
+        return compute_opportunity_score(self.importance, self.satisfaction)
+
+
+class BusinessValue(BaseModel):
+    category: BusinessImpactCategory
+    statement: str
+    detail: str | None = None
+    estimated_annual_value: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0.0)
+    confidence: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0.0, le=1.0)
+
+
+class CustomerOutcome(BaseModel):
+    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
+    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this outcome relates to")
+    step_id: str | None = Field(
+        default=None, description="The ID of the specific Step, if applicable"
+    )
+    customer_value: CustomerValue
+    business_value: BusinessValue
+
+    @computed_field
+    @property
+    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
+        return self.customer_value.opportunity_score

+"""Repository interfaces and in-memory implementation."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Protocol
+
+from agentic_odi_core.models import CustomerOutcome, Job, Outcome, Step
+
+
+class Repository(Protocol):
+    def add_job(self, job: Job) -> Job: ...
+    def list_jobs(self) -> list[Job]: ...
+    def get_job(self, job_id: str) -> Job | None: ...
+    def add_step(self, step: Step) -> Step: ...
+    def get_steps_for_job(self, job_id: str) -> list[Step]: ...
+    def add_outcome(self, outcome: Outcome) -> Outcome: ...
+    def get_outcomes(self, job_id: str, step_id: str | None = None) -> list[Outcome]: ...
+    def add_customer_outcome(self, co: CustomerOutcome) -> CustomerOutcome: ...
+    def get_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> CustomerOutcome | None: ...
+    def list_customer_outcomes(self, job_id: str | None = None) -> list[CustomerOutcome]: ...
+    def update_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str, updates: dict) -> CustomerOutcome | None: ...
+    def delete_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> bool: ...
+    def clear(self) -> None: ...
+
+
+class InMemoryRepository:
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.jobs: dict[str, Job] = {}
+        self.steps: dict[str, Step] = {}
+        self.outcomes: dict[str, Outcome] = {}
+        self.customer_outcomes: dict[str, CustomerOutcome] = {}
+
+    def add_job(self, job: Job) -> Job:
+        self.jobs[job.id] = job
+        return job
+
+    def list_jobs(self) -> list[Job]:
+        return list(self.jobs.values())
+
+    def get_job(self, job_id: str) -> Job | None:
+        return self.jobs.get(job_id)
+
+    def add_step(self, step: Step) -> Step:
+        self.steps[step.id] = step
+        return step
+
+    def get_steps_for_job(self, job_id: str) -> list[Step]:
+        return [s for s in self.steps.values() if s.job_id == job_id]
+
+    def add_outcome(self, outcome: Outcome) -> Outcome:
+        self.outcomes[outcome.id] = outcome
+        return outcome
+
+    def get_outcomes(self, job_id: str, step_id: str | None = None) -> list[Outcome]:
+        outs = [o for o in self.outcomes.values() if o.job_id == job_id]
+        if step_id is not None:
+            outs = [o for o in outs if o.step_id == step_id]
+        return outs
+
+    def add_customer_outcome(self, co: CustomerOutcome) -> CustomerOutcome:
+        self.customer_outcomes[co.id] = co
+        return co
+
+    def get_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> CustomerOutcome | None:
+        return self.customer_outcomes.get(outcome_id)
+
+    def list_customer_outcomes(self, job_id: str | None = None) -> list[CustomerOutcome]:
+        if job_id is None:
+            return list(self.customer_outcomes.values())
+        return [co for co in self.customer_outcomes.values() if co.job_id == job_id]
+
+    def update_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str, updates: dict) -> CustomerOutcome | None:
+        co = self.customer_outcomes.get(outcome_id)
+        if not co:
+            return None
+        current = co.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
+        current.update(updates)
+        new_co = co.model_validate(current)
+        self.customer_outcomes[outcome_id] = new_co
+        return new_co
+
+    def delete_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> bool:
+        if outcome_id in self.customer_outcomes:
+            del self.customer_outcomes[outcome_id]
+            return True
+        return False
+
+    def clear(self) -> None:
+        self.jobs.clear()
+        self.steps.clear()
+        self.outcomes.clear()
+        self.customer_outcomes.clear()

+"""Service layer implementing business logic."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import uuid
+from typing import Any
+
+from agentic_odi_core.models import (
+    BusinessValue,
+    CustomerOutcome,
+    CustomerValue,
+    Job,
+    Outcome,
+    Step,
+    compute_opportunity_score,
+)
+from agentic_odi_core.repository import Repository
+
+
+class JobNotFoundError(Exception):
+    def __init__(self, job_id: str) -> None:
+        self.job_id = job_id
+        super().__init__(job_id)
+
+
+class CustomerOutcomeNotFoundError(Exception):
+    def __init__(self, outcome_id: str) -> None:
+        self.outcome_id = outcome_id
+        super().__init__(outcome_id)
+
+
+class ValueOutOfRangeError(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+class ODIService:
+    def __init__(self, repo: Repository) -> None:
+        self.repo = repo
+
+    def add_job(self, name: str, description: str | None = None) -> Job:
+        job = Job(name=name, description=description)
+        return self.repo.add_job(job)
+
+    def get_jobs(self) -> list[Job]:
+        return self.repo.list_jobs()
+
+    def get_job(self, job_id: str) -> Job | None:
+        return self.repo.get_job(job_id)
+
+    def add_step(self, job_id: str, name: str, order: int) -> Step:
+        step = Step(id=str(uuid.uuid4()), job_id=job_id, name=name, order=order)
+        return self.repo.add_step(step)
+
+    def get_job_map(self, job_id: str) -> list[Step]:
+        steps = self.repo.get_steps_for_job(job_id)
+        return sorted(steps, key=lambda s: s.order)
+
+    def add_outcome(
+        self,
+        job_id: str,
+        statement: str,
+        importance: float | None = None,
+        satisfaction: float | None = None,
+        step_id: str | None = None,
+    ) -> Outcome:
+        if importance is not None and not (1.0 <= importance <= 10.0):
+            raise ValueOutOfRangeError()
+        if satisfaction is not None and not (1.0 <= satisfaction <= 10.0):
+            raise ValueOutOfRangeError()
+        opportunity_score = None
+        if importance is not None and satisfaction is not None:
+            opportunity_score = compute_opportunity_score(importance, satisfaction)
+        outcome = Outcome(
+            id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
+            job_id=job_id,
+            step_id=step_id,
+            statement=statement,
+            importance=importance,
+            satisfaction=satisfaction,
+            opportunity_score=opportunity_score,
+        )
+        return self.repo.add_outcome(outcome)
+
+    def get_outcomes(self, job_id: str, step_id: str | None = None) -> list[Outcome]:
+        return self.repo.get_outcomes(job_id, step_id)
+
+    def add_customer_outcome(
+        self,
+        job_id: str,
+        customer_value: CustomerValue | dict[str, Any],
+        business_value: BusinessValue | dict[str, Any],
+        step_id: str | None = None,
+    ) -> CustomerOutcome:
+        if isinstance(customer_value, dict):
+            cv = CustomerValue.model_validate(customer_value)
+        else:
+            cv = customer_value
+        if isinstance(business_value, dict):
+            bv = BusinessValue.model_validate(business_value)
+        else:
+            bv = business_value
+        co = CustomerOutcome(
+            id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
+            job_id=job_id,
+            step_id=step_id,
+            customer_value=cv,
+            business_value=bv,
+        )
+        return self.repo.add_customer_outcome(co)
+
+    def get_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> CustomerOutcome:
+        co = self.repo.get_customer_outcome(outcome_id)
+        if not co:
+            raise CustomerOutcomeNotFoundError(outcome_id)
+        return co
+
+    def list_customer_outcomes(self, job_id: str | None = None) -> list[CustomerOutcome]:
+        return self.repo.list_customer_outcomes(job_id)
+
+    def update_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str, updates: dict[str, Any]) -> CustomerOutcome:
+        res = self.repo.update_customer_outcome(outcome_id, updates)
+        if not res:
+            raise CustomerOutcomeNotFoundError(outcome_id)
+        return res
+
+    def delete_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> None:
+        ok = self.repo.delete_customer_outcome(outcome_id)
+        if not ok:
+            raise CustomerOutcomeNotFoundError(outcome_id)
+
+    def compute_opportunity(self, importance: float, satisfaction: float) -> float:
+        return compute_opportunity_score(importance, satisfaction)

@@ -0,0 +1,124 @@
+"""SQLite-backed repository using append-only IntentStore for events/audit."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+from typing import Any
+
+from pydantic import ValidationError
+
+from agentic_odi_core.intent_store import IntentStore
+from agentic_odi_core.models import CustomerOutcome, Job, Outcome, Step
+from agentic_odi_core.repository import Repository
+
+
+class SQLiteRepository(Repository):
+    def __init__(self, db_path: str | None = None) -> None:
+        if db_path is None:
+            db_path = os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_DB", os.path.expanduser("~/.agentic-odi/odi.db"))
+        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(db_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
+        self.store = IntentStore(db_path)
+        # For compatibility with existing semantics, we also maintain a materialized
+        # view in memory for fast reads (in-memory snapshot) - simple approach for now.
+        self._load_snapshot()
+
+    def _load_snapshot(self) -> None:
+        self.jobs: dict[str, Job] = {}
+        self.steps: dict[str, Step] = {}
+        self.outcomes: dict[str, Outcome] = {}
+        self.customer_outcomes: dict[str, CustomerOutcome] = {}
+        for ev in self.store.get_stream():
+            et = ev["type"]
+            p = ev["payload"]
+            if et == "JOB_CREATED":
+                self.jobs[p["id"]] = Job.model_validate(p)
+            elif et == "STEP_CREATED":
+                self.steps[p["id"]] = Step.model_validate(p)
+            elif et == "OUTCOME_CREATED":
+                self.outcomes[p["id"]] = Outcome.model_validate(p)
+            elif et == "CUSTOMER_OUTCOME_CREATED":
+                self.customer_outcomes[p["id"]] = CustomerOutcome.model_validate(p)
+            elif et == "CUSTOMER_OUTCOME_UPDATED":
+                cid = p["id"]
+                co = self.customer_outcomes.get(cid)
+                if co is not None:
+                    current = co.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
+                    current.update(p.get("updates", {}))
+                    try:
+                        self.customer_outcomes[cid] = co.model_validate(current)
+                    except ValidationError:
+                        pass
+            elif et == "CUSTOMER_OUTCOME_DELETED":
+                cid = p["id"]
+                self.customer_outcomes.pop(cid, None)
+        # also snapshot jobs/steps/outcomes? we emitted above
+
+    def add_job(self, job: Job) -> Job:
+        self.store.append("JOB_CREATED", job.model_dump())
+        self.jobs[job.id] = job
+        return job
+
+    def list_jobs(self) -> list[Job]:
+        return list(self.jobs.values())
+
+    def get_job(self, job_id: str) -> Job | None:
+        return self.jobs.get(job_id)
+
+    def add_step(self, step: Step) -> Step:
+        self.store.append("STEP_CREATED", step.model_dump())
+        self.steps[step.id] = step
+        return step
+
+    def get_steps_for_job(self, job_id: str) -> list[Step]:
+        return [s for s in self.steps.values() if s.job_id == job_id]
+
+    def add_outcome(self, outcome: Outcome) -> Outcome:
+        self.store.append("OUTCOME_CREATED", outcome.model_dump())
+        self.outcomes[outcome.id] = outcome
+        return outcome
+
+    def get_outcomes(self, job_id: str, step_id: str | None = None) -> list[Outcome]:
+        outs = [o for o in self.outcomes.values() if o.job_id == job_id]
+        if step_id is not None:
+            outs = [o for o in outs if o.step_id == step_id]
+        return outs
+
+    def add_customer_outcome(self, co: CustomerOutcome) -> CustomerOutcome:
+        self.store.append("CUSTOMER_OUTCOME_CREATED", co.model_dump())
+        self.customer_outcomes[co.id] = co
+        return co
+
+    def get_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> CustomerOutcome | None:
+        return self.customer_outcomes.get(outcome_id)
+
+    def list_customer_outcomes(self, job_id: str | None = None) -> list[CustomerOutcome]:
+        if job_id is None:
+            return list(self.customer_outcomes.values())
+        return [co for co in self.customer_outcomes.values() if co.job_id == job_id]
+
+    def update_customer_outcome(
+        self, outcome_id: str, updates: dict[str, Any]
+    ) -> CustomerOutcome | None:
+        co = self.customer_outcomes.get(outcome_id)
+        if not co:
+            return None
+        current = co.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
+        current.update(updates)
+        try:
+            new_co = co.model_validate(current)
+        except ValidationError:
+            return None
+        self.store.append("CUSTOMER_OUTCOME_UPDATED", {"id": outcome_id, "updates": updates})
+        self.customer_outcomes[outcome_id] = new_co
+        return new_co
+
+    def delete_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> bool:
+        if outcome_id in self.customer_outcomes:
+            self.store.append("CUSTOMER_OUTCOME_DELETED", {"id": outcome_id})
+            del self.customer_outcomes[outcome_id]
+            return True
+        return False
+
+    def clear(self) -> None:
+        self.store.clear()
+        self._load_snapshot()

+"""Tests for the append-only Intent Store."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+

+
+def test_append_and_get_stream_return_events_in_order(tmp_path) -> None:
+    store = IntentStore(str(tmp_path / "events.db"))
+    try:
+        store.append("JOB_CREATED", {"id": "job-1"})
+        store.append("STEP_CREATED", {"id": "step-1", "job_id": "job-1"})
+
+        stream = store.get_stream()
+    finally:
+        store.close()
+
+    assert [event["type"] for event in stream] == ["JOB_CREATED", "STEP_CREATED"]
+    assert [event["payload"] for event in stream] == [
+        {"id": "job-1"},
+        {"id": "step-1", "job_id": "job-1"},
+    ]
+    assert [event["id"] for event in stream] == [1, 2]
+    assert all(event["timestamp"] for event in stream)
+
+
+def test_clear_removes_every_event(tmp_path) -> None:
+    store = IntentStore(str(tmp_path / "events.db"))
+    try:
+        store.append("JOB_CREATED", {"id": "job-1"})
+        store.clear()
+        assert store.get_stream() == []
+    finally:
+        store.close()
+
+
+def test_get_stream_treats_blank_payload_as_empty_dict(tmp_path) -> None:

+def test_add_and_get_job(service: ODIService) -> None:

+    assert service.get_jobs() == [job]

+def test_get_job_returns_none_for_unknown_id(service: ODIService) -> None:

+    assert repo.get_job("missing") is None
+    assert repo.get_steps_for_job("job-1") == [step]
+    assert repo.get_outcomes("job-1") == [outcome]

+    assert repo.list_customer_outcomes() == [customer_outcome]

+    assert repo.list_customer_outcomes("other") == []
+
+
+def test_snapshot_reloads_every_event_type_from_disk(tmp_path) -> None:
+    db_path = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")

+    repo.add_step(Step(id="step-1", job_id="job-1", name="Prepare", order=1))
+    repo.add_outcome(Outcome(id="outcome-1", job_id="job-1", statement="Minimize time"))
+    created = repo.add_customer_outcome(_customer_outcome("job-1"))
+    customer_value = created.customer_value.model_dump()
+    customer_value["importance"] = 9.0
+    repo.update_customer_outcome("co-1", {"customer_value": customer_value})
+
+    reloaded = SQLiteRepository(db_path)
+
+    assert reloaded.get_job("job-1") is not None
+    assert reloaded.get_steps_for_job("job-1")[0].name == "Prepare"
+    assert reloaded.get_outcomes("job-1")[0].statement == "Minimize time"
+    reloaded_outcome = reloaded.get_customer_outcome("co-1")
+    assert reloaded_outcome is not None
+    assert reloaded_outcome.customer_value.importance == 9.0

 #!/usr/bin/env bash
 #
 # Build a self-contained, onedir PyInstaller bundle of the `odi` CLI and
 # package it into a distributable archive at the repository root.
 #
 # Environment:
 #   VERSION            required, e.g. 0.1.0
 #   RELEASE_DATE_UTC   optional, e.g. 2026-10-15T21:13:00Z (default: "")
 #   COMMIT             optional (default: dev)
 #   TARGET             optional, e.g. linux_x86_64 (default: dev)
 #
 # The absolute path of the produced archive is printed on the last line.
 set -euo pipefail
 
 export UV_PYTHON="${UV_PYTHON:-3.11}"
 
 REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
 cd "$REPO_ROOT"
 
 VERSION="${VERSION:?VERSION is required}"
 RELEASE_DATE_UTC="${RELEASE_DATE_UTC:-}"
 COMMIT="${COMMIT:-dev}"
 TARGET="${TARGET:-dev}"
 
 # _build_info.py is tracked with committed dev defaults; the build regenerates
 # it from the environment. Back it up and always restore it on exit (even on
 # failure) so a build never leaves the working tree dirty.
-BUILD_INFO="cli/src/cli/_build_info.py"
+BUILD_INFO="apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/_build_info.py"
 BUILD_INFO_BACKUP="$(mktemp)"
 cp "$BUILD_INFO" "$BUILD_INFO_BACKUP"
 restore_build_info() {
     cp "$BUILD_INFO_BACKUP" "$BUILD_INFO"
     rm -f "$BUILD_INFO_BACKUP"
 }
 trap restore_build_info EXIT
 
 echo "==> Syncing workspace (uv)"
 uv sync --all-packages --locked
 
-echo "==> Writing cli/src/cli/_build_info.py"
-cat > cli/src/cli/_build_info.py <<EOF
+echo "==> Writing apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/_build_info.py"
+cat > apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/_build_info.py <<EOF
 VERSION = "${VERSION}"
 RELEASE_DATE_UTC = "${RELEASE_DATE_UTC}"
 COMMIT = "${COMMIT}"
 TARGET = "${TARGET}"
 EOF
 
 echo "==> Running PyInstaller"
-uv run --directory cli pyinstaller --clean --noconfirm \
-    --distpath ../dist --workpath ../build/odi \
-    ../packaging/pyinstaller/odi.spec
+uv run pyinstaller --clean --noconfirm \
+    --distpath dist --workpath build/odi \
+    packaging/pyinstaller/odi.spec
 
 ARCHIVE_NAME="odi_${VERSION}_${TARGET}"
 if [[ "$TARGET" == windows* ]]; then
     rm -f "${ARCHIVE_NAME}.zip"
     (cd dist/odi && zip -r -q "../../${ARCHIVE_NAME}.zip" .)
     ARCHIVE_PATH="${REPO_ROOT}/${ARCHIVE_NAME}.zip"
 else
     rm -f "${ARCHIVE_NAME}.tar.gz"
     tar -C dist/odi -czf "${ARCHIVE_NAME}.tar.gz" .
     ARCHIVE_PATH="${REPO_ROOT}/${ARCHIVE_NAME}.tar.gz"
 fi
 
 echo "$ARCHIVE_PATH"
