name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Ruff Lint (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff check .

      - name: Verify Ruff Formatting (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Mypy (core)
        run: uv run --directory core mypy .

      - name: Run Mypy (mcp_server)
        run: uv run --directory mcp_server mypy .

      - name: Run Mypy (local_server)
        run: uv run --directory local_server mypy .

      - name: Run Mypy (cli)
        run: uv run --directory cli mypy .

      - name: Run Mypy (client)
        run: uv run --directory client mypy .

      - name: Run Mypy (connectors)
        run: uv run --directory connectors mypy .

      - name: Run Mypy (website)
        run: uv run --directory website mypy .

  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Bandit
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r core/src mcp_server/src local_server/src cli/src client/src connectors/src

      - name: Run Bandit (website)
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r website/

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Pytest (core)
        run: uv run --directory core pytest --cov=core --cov-report=term-missing
        env:
          COVERAGE_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.core

      - name: Pytest (mcp_server)
        run: uv run --directory mcp_server pytest --cov=mcp_server --cov-report=term-missing
        env:
          COVERAGE_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.mcp_server

      - name: Pytest (local_server)
        run: uv run --directory local_server pytest --cov=local_server --cov-report=term-missing
        env:
          COVERAGE_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.local_server

      - name: Pytest (cli)
        run: uv run --directory cli pytest --cov=cli --cov-report=term-missing
        env:
          COVERAGE_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.cli

      - name: Pytest (client)
        run: uv run --directory client pytest --cov=client --cov-report=term-missing
        env:
          COVERAGE_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.client

      - name: Pytest (connectors)
        run: uv run --directory connectors pytest --cov=connectors --cov-report=term-missing
        env:
          COVERAGE_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.connectors

      - name: Combine and report coverage
        run: |
          unset COVERAGE_FILE
          uv run coverage combine \
            "${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.core" \
            "${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.mcp_server" \
            "${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.local_server" \
            "${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.cli" \
            "${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.client" \
            "${{ github.workspace }}/.coverage.connectors"
          uv run coverage xml -o "${{ github.workspace }}/coverage.xml"
          uv run coverage report

      - name: Upload coverage report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: coverage.xml
          if-no-files-found: error

      # One upload per run is enough; the 3.12 report is the canonical one.
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ matrix.python-version == '3.12' }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: coverage.xml
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: CLI reports a version
        run: |
          version="$(uv run python -m cli --version)"
          [ -n "$version" ]
          echo "OK: $version"

      - name: CLI exposes connectors commands
        run: |
          help="$(uv run python -m cli connectors --help)"
          echo "$help" | grep -q list
          echo "$help" | grep -q ingest
          echo "OK: connectors help"

      - name: Installer installs from a simulated release
        run: bash scripts/tests/install_e2e.sh

      - name: MCP server boots and serves /mcp
        run: |
          uv run python -m mcp_server > /tmp/mcp_server.log 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sfX POST http://localhost:8000/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
              -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "MCP server did not respond on :8000/mcp"
            cat /tmp/mcp_server.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: MCP server responded with 200"

      - name: Living Studio sidecar serves the studio API
        run: |
          uv run python -m local_server.main > /tmp/sidecar.log 2>&1 &
          SIDECAR_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/health/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"mcp_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp"}' -o /dev/null &&
              curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/canvas?mcp_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp" -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "Living Studio sidecar did not respond on :8100"
            cat /tmp/sidecar.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: sidecar studio API responded with 200"

      - name: python -m client.run brings up both services and stops cleanly
        run: |
          uv run python -m client.run > /tmp/clientrun.log 2>&1 &
          RUN_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/config &&
              curl -sfX POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp \
                -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
                -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "client.run did not bring up both services"
            cat /tmp/clientrun.log
            kill "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 1
          fi
          kill -INT "$RUN_PID"
          wait "$RUN_PID"
          echo "OK: both services stopped cleanly"

  website:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Pytest (website)
        run: uv run --directory website pytest tests/

      - name: Build site (rsync)
        run: |
          mkdir -p _site
          rsync -av website/ _site/ --exclude='tests/' --exclude='tools/'

  studio:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: studio
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: studio/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Unit tests
        run: npm test -- --run

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Verify generated API types are up to date
        run: |
          npm run gen:api-types
          git diff --exit-code -- src/api/schema.d.ts

  tauri-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: studio/src-tauri
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Cargo fmt
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: Cargo clippy
        run: cargo clippy -- -D warnings

      - name: Cargo check
        run: cargo check

  tauri-build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: studio/package-lock.json

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: npm ci
        working-directory: studio

      - name: Configure updater artifacts
        working-directory: studio
        env:
          SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo 'TAURI_CONFIG={"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}' >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "No TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY provided — building without signed updater artifacts."
          fi

      - name: Build desktop bundle
        working-directory: studio
        env:
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: npm run tauri build

      - name: Upload desktop bundles
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: tauri-bundles-linux
          if-no-files-found: warn
          path: |
            studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/*.deb
            studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage
            studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage.sig

  ci-green:
    name: CI green
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test, smoke, website, studio, tauri-check, tauri-build]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Verify all required jobs succeeded
        run: |
          results='${{ join(needs.*.result, ' ') }}'
          echo "Job results: $results"
          for result in $results; do
            if [ "$result" != "success" ]; then
              echo "::error::A required job did not succeed ($results)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "OK: all required jobs succeeded"

              curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/canvas?mcp_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp" -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "Living Studio sidecar did not respond on :8100"
            cat /tmp/sidecar.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: sidecar studio API responded with 200"

      - name: scripts/dev.py brings up both services and stops cleanly
        run: |
          uv run python scripts/dev.py > /tmp/clientrun.log 2>&1 &
          RUN_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/config &&
              curl -sfX POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp \
                -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
                -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "scripts/dev.py did not bring up both services"
            cat /tmp/clientrun.log
            kill "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 1
          fi
          kill -INT "$RUN_PID"
          wait "$RUN_PID"
          echo "OK: both services stopped cleanly"

  website:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Pytest (website)
        run: uv run --directory website pytest tests/

      - name: Build site (rsync)
        run: |
          mkdir -p _site
          rsync -av website/ _site/ --exclude='tests/' --exclude='tools/'

  studio:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Unit tests
        run: npm test -- --run

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Verify generated API types are up to date
        run: |
          npm run gen:api-types
          git diff --exit-code -- src/api/schema.d.ts

  tauri-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio/src-tauri
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Cargo fmt
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: Cargo clippy
        run: cargo clippy -- -D warnings

      - name: Cargo check
        run: cargo check

  tauri-build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: npm ci
        working-directory: apps/studio

      - name: Configure updater artifacts
        working-directory: apps/studio
        env:
          SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo 'TAURI_CONFIG={"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}' >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "No TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY provided — building without signed updater artifacts."
          fi

      - name: Build desktop bundle
        working-directory: apps/studio
        env:
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: npm run tauri build

      - name: Upload desktop bundles
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: tauri-bundles-linux
          if-no-files-found: warn
          path: |
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/*.deb
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage.sig

  ci-green:
    name: CI green
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test, smoke, website, studio, tauri-check, tauri-build]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Verify all required jobs succeeded
        run: |
          results='${{ join(needs.*.result, ' ') }}'
          echo "Job results: $results"
          for result in $results; do
            if [ "$result" != "success" ]; then
              echo "::error::A required job did not succeed ($results)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "OK: all required jobs succeeded"

  python-version:
    description: Python version to install and use.
    required: false

  preflight:

    timeout-minutes: 10

      - name: Require updater signing key
        env:
          SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$SIGNING_KEY" ]; then

          - platform: windows-latest

# -*- mode: python ; coding: utf-8 -*-
"""PyInstaller onedir spec for the odi CLI.

Run from the repository root, e.g.::

    uv run pyinstaller --clean --noconfirm \
        --distpath dist --workpath build/odi \
        packaging/pyinstaller/odi.spec
"""

import os

from PyInstaller.utils.hooks import collect_all

_spec_dir = os.path.abspath(SPECPATH)
_repo_root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(_spec_dir))
_cli_src = os.path.join(_repo_root, "apps", "cli", "src")
_entry = os.path.join(_cli_src, "agentic_odi_cli", "__main__.py")

datas = []
binaries = []
hiddenimports = []

for _pkg in (
    "fastmcp",
    "mcp",
    "pydantic",
    "pydantic_core",
    "starlette",
    "uvicorn",
    "anyio",
):
    _pkg_datas, _pkg_binaries, _pkg_hiddenimports = collect_all(_pkg)
    datas += _pkg_datas
    binaries += _pkg_binaries
    hiddenimports += _pkg_hiddenimports

hiddenimports += [
    "agentic_odi_connectors",
    "agentic_odi_core",
    "agentic_odi_cli",
    "agentic_odi_cli.cli",
    "agentic_odi_cli.backend",
    "agentic_odi_cli.chat",
    "agentic_odi_cli.connectors",
    "agentic_odi_cli.context",
    "agentic_odi_cli.customer_outcomes",
    "agentic_odi_cli.onboard",
    "agentic_odi_cli.paths",
    "agentic_odi_cli.profile",
    "agentic_odi_cli.render",
    "agentic_odi_cli.update",
    "agentic_odi_cli.version",
    "agentic_odi_cli._build_info",
]

# Heavy optional dependencies pulled in transitively by fastmcp's optional
# extras (e.g. the ``apps``/``openai`` extras and pydantic's mypy plugin).
# The CLI never exercises these code paths and bundling them inflates the
# onedir payload by ~250 MB, so drop them.
_excludes = [
    "IPython",
    "altair",
    "matplotlib",
    "mypy",
    "narwhals",
    "numpy",
    "openai",
    "pandas",
    "PIL",
    "pyarrow",
    "pytest",
    "streamlit",
    "tkinter",
]

a = Analysis(
    [_entry],
    pathex=[_cli_src],
    binaries=binaries,
    datas=datas,
    hiddenimports=hiddenimports,
    hookspath=[],
    hooksconfig={},
    runtime_hooks=[],
    excludes=_excludes,
    noarchive=False,
)

pyz = PYZ(a.pure)

exe = EXE(
    pyz,
    a.scripts,
    [],
    exclude_binaries=True,
    name="odi",
    debug=False,
    bootloader_ignore_signals=False,
    strip=False,
    upx=False,
    console=True,
    disable_windowed_traceback=False,
    argv_emulation=False,
    target_arch=None,
    codesign_identity=None,
    entitlements_file=None,
)

coll = COLLECT(
    exe,
    a.binaries,
    a.datas,
    strip=False,
    upx=False,
    upx_exclude=[],
    name="odi",
)
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Build a self-contained, onedir PyInstaller bundle of the `odi` CLI and
# package it into a distributable archive at the repository root.
#
# Environment:
#   VERSION            required, e.g. 0.1.0
#   RELEASE_DATE_UTC   optional, e.g. 2026-10-15T21:13:00Z (default: "")
#   COMMIT             optional (default: dev)
#   TARGET             optional, e.g. linux_x86_64 (default: dev)
#
# The absolute path of the produced archive is printed on the last line.
set -euo pipefail

export UV_PYTHON="${UV_PYTHON:-3.11}"

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"

VERSION="${VERSION:?VERSION is required}"
RELEASE_DATE_UTC="${RELEASE_DATE_UTC:-}"
COMMIT="${COMMIT:-dev}"
TARGET="${TARGET:-dev}"

# _build_info.py is tracked with committed dev defaults; the build regenerates
# it from the environment. Back it up and always restore it on exit (even on
# failure) so a build never leaves the working tree dirty.
BUILD_INFO="apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/_build_info.py"
BUILD_INFO_BACKUP="$(mktemp)"
cp "$BUILD_INFO" "$BUILD_INFO_BACKUP"
restore_build_info() {
    cp "$BUILD_INFO_BACKUP" "$BUILD_INFO"
    rm -f "$BUILD_INFO_BACKUP"
}
trap restore_build_info EXIT

echo "==> Syncing workspace (uv)"
uv sync --all-packages --locked

echo "==> Writing apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/_build_info.py"
cat > apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/_build_info.py <<EOF
VERSION = "${VERSION}"
RELEASE_DATE_UTC = "${RELEASE_DATE_UTC}"
COMMIT = "${COMMIT}"
TARGET = "${TARGET}"
EOF

echo "==> Running PyInstaller"
uv run pyinstaller --clean --noconfirm \
    --distpath dist --workpath build/odi \
    packaging/pyinstaller/odi.spec

ARCHIVE_NAME="odi_${VERSION}_${TARGET}"
if [[ "$TARGET" == windows* ]]; then
    rm -f "${ARCHIVE_NAME}.zip"
    (cd dist/odi && zip -r -q "../../${ARCHIVE_NAME}.zip" .)
    ARCHIVE_PATH="${REPO_ROOT}/${ARCHIVE_NAME}.zip"
else
    rm -f "${ARCHIVE_NAME}.tar.gz"
    tar -C dist/odi -czf "${ARCHIVE_NAME}.tar.gz" .
    ARCHIVE_PATH="${REPO_ROOT}/${ARCHIVE_NAME}.tar.gz"
fi

echo "$ARCHIVE_PATH"

# -*- mode: python ; coding: utf-8 -*-
"""PyInstaller onedir spec for the odi CLI.

Run from the repository root, e.g.::

    uv run pyinstaller --clean --noconfirm \
        --distpath dist --workpath build/odi \
        packaging/pyinstaller/odi.spec
"""

import os

from PyInstaller.utils.hooks import collect_all

_spec_dir = os.path.abspath(SPECPATH)
_repo_root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(_spec_dir))
_cli_src = os.path.join(_repo_root, "apps", "cli", "src")
_entry = os.path.join(_cli_src, "agentic_odi_cli", "__main__.py")

datas = []
binaries = []
hiddenimports = []

for _pkg in (
    "fastmcp",
    "mcp",
    "pydantic",
    "pydantic_core",
    "starlette",
    "uvicorn",
    "anyio",
):
    _pkg_datas, _pkg_binaries, _pkg_hiddenimports = collect_all(_pkg)
    datas += _pkg_datas
    binaries += _pkg_binaries
    hiddenimports += _pkg_hiddenimports

hiddenimports += [
    "agentic_odi_connectors",
    "agentic_odi_core",
    "agentic_odi_cli",
    "agentic_odi_cli.cli",
    "agentic_odi_cli.backend",
    "agentic_odi_cli.chat",
    "agentic_odi_cli.connectors",
    "agentic_odi_cli.context",
    "agentic_odi_cli.customer_outcomes",
    "agentic_odi_cli.onboard",
    "agentic_odi_cli.paths",
    "agentic_odi_cli.profile",
    "agentic_odi_cli.render",
    "agentic_odi_cli.update",
    "agentic_odi_cli.version",
    "agentic_odi_cli._build_info",
]

# Heavy optional dependencies pulled in transitively by fastmcp's optional
# extras (e.g. the ``apps``/``openai`` extras and pydantic's mypy plugin).
# The CLI never exercises these code paths and bundling them inflates the
# onedir payload by ~250 MB, so drop them.
_excludes = [
    "IPython",
    "altair",
    "matplotlib",
    "mypy",
    "narwhals",
    "numpy",
    "openai",
    "pandas",
    "PIL",
    "pyarrow",
    "pytest",
    "streamlit",
    "tkinter",
]

a = Analysis(
    [_entry],
    pathex=[_cli_src],
    binaries=binaries,
    datas=datas,
    hiddenimports=hiddenimports,
    hookspath=[],
    hooksconfig={},
    runtime_hooks=[],
    excludes=_excludes,
    noarchive=False,
)

pyz = PYZ(a.pure)

exe = EXE(
    pyz,
    a.scripts,
    [],
    exclude_binaries=True,
    name="odi",
    debug=False,
    bootloader_ignore_signals=False,
    strip=False,
    upx=False,
    console=True,
    disable_windowed_traceback=False,
    argv_emulation=False,
    target_arch=None,
    codesign_identity=None,
    entitlements_file=None,
)

coll = COLLECT(
    exe,
    a.binaries,
    a.datas,
    strip=False,
    upx=False,
    upx_exclude=[],
    name="odi",
)
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Build a self-contained, onedir PyInstaller bundle of the `odi` CLI and
# package it into a distributable archive at the repository root.
#
# Environment:
#   VERSION            required, e.g. 0.1.0
#   RELEASE_DATE_UTC   optional, e.g. 2026-10-15T21:13:00Z (default: "")
#   COMMIT             optional (default: dev)
#   TARGET             optional, e.g. linux_x86_64 (default: dev)
#
# The absolute path of the produced archive is printed on the last line.
set -euo pipefail

export UV_PYTHON="${UV_PYTHON:-3.11}"

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"

VERSION="${VERSION:?VERSION is required}"
RELEASE_DATE_UTC="${RELEASE_DATE_UTC:-}"
COMMIT="${COMMIT:-dev}"
TARGET="${TARGET:-dev}"

# _build_info.py is tracked with committed dev defaults; the build regenerates
# it from the environment. Back it up and always restore it on exit (even on
# failure) so a build never leaves the working tree dirty.
BUILD_INFO="apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/_build_info.py"
BUILD_INFO_BACKUP="$(mktemp)"
cp "$BUILD_INFO" "$BUILD_INFO_BACKUP"
restore_build_info() {
    cp "$BUILD_INFO_BACKUP" "$BUILD_INFO"
    rm -f "$BUILD_INFO_BACKUP"
}
trap restore_build_info EXIT

echo "==> Syncing workspace (uv)"
uv sync --all-packages --locked

echo "==> Writing apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/_build_info.py"
cat > apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/_build_info.py <<EOF
VERSION = "${VERSION}"
RELEASE_DATE_UTC = "${RELEASE_DATE_UTC}"
COMMIT = "${COMMIT}"
TARGET = "${TARGET}"
EOF

echo "==> Running PyInstaller"
uv run pyinstaller --clean --noconfirm \
    --distpath dist --workpath build/odi \
    packaging/pyinstaller/odi.spec

ARCHIVE_NAME="odi_${VERSION}_${TARGET}"
if [[ "$TARGET" == windows* ]]; then
    rm -f "${ARCHIVE_NAME}.zip"
    (cd dist/odi && zip -r -q "../../${ARCHIVE_NAME}.zip" .)
    ARCHIVE_PATH="${REPO_ROOT}/${ARCHIVE_NAME}.zip"
else
    rm -f "${ARCHIVE_NAME}.tar.gz"
    tar -C dist/odi -czf "${ARCHIVE_NAME}.tar.gz" .
    ARCHIVE_PATH="${REPO_ROOT}/${ARCHIVE_NAME}.tar.gz"
fi

echo "$ARCHIVE_PATH"

"""Keep the live MCP surface in lockstep with the core contract."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
from agentic_odi_core.contract import TOOL_SPECS
from agentic_odi_mcp_server.mcp_server import mcp
from fastmcp import Client


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_mcp_exposes_exactly_the_contract_tools() -> None:
    async with Client(mcp) as client:
        tools = await client.list_tools()

    assert {tool.name for tool in tools} == set(TOOL_SPECS)


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_mcp_argument_names_match_the_contract() -> None:
    async with Client(mcp) as client:
        tools = {tool.name: tool for tool in await client.list_tools()}

    for name, spec in TOOL_SPECS.items():
        schema = tools[name].input_schema
        assert set(schema.get("properties", {})) == set(spec.arguments), name
        assert set(schema.get("required", [])) == set(spec.required), name

from agentic_odi_cli.backend import _LOCAL_HANDLERS

LOCAL_TOOLS = {

    "get_customer_outcome",
    "list_customer_outcomes",
    "update_customer_outcome",
    "delete_customer_outcome",
    "compute_opportunity",
}


def test_local_handler_keys_are_contract_tools() -> None:
    assert set(_LOCAL_HANDLERS) == LOCAL_TOOLS
    assert LOCAL_TOOLS <= set(TOOL_NAMES)

# website/tests/test_site.py
import re
from html.parser import HTMLParser
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
SITE = ROOT / "website"
PAGES_URL = "https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/"

ALLOWED_EXTERNAL = {
    "https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi",
    "https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/issues",
    "https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat",
    "https://docs.astral.sh/uv/",
    "https://modelcontextprotocol.io",
    PAGES_URL,
}

MILESTONE_DATE = re.compile(
    r"\b(Q[1-4]|Jan(uary)?|Feb(ruary)?|Mar(ch)?|Apr(il)?|May|Jun(e)?|"
    r"Jul(y)?|Aug(ust)?|Sep(t(ember)?)?|Oct(ober)?|Nov(ember)?|Dec(ember)?)[ -]20\d\d\b"
)

EMOJI = re.compile("[\u2600-\u27bf\U0001f300-\U0001faff]")


class Doc(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.lang = None
        self.charset = False
        self.viewport = False
        self.title = ""
        self.ids: set[str] = set()
        self.hrefs: list[str] = []
        self.refs: list[str] = []
        self.headings: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
        self.tags: list[str] = []
        self.metas: dict[str, str] = {}
        self.theme_colors: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    assert "experimental" in low
    assert "free prefect account" in low
    assert "all rights reserved" in low
    assert "strategyn" in low
    assert "your roadmap is a guess." in low
    assert "we don't publish dates" in low
    assert "open an issue" in low
    assert "http://localhost:8000/mcp" in text
    assert "agentic-odi.fastmcp.app" not in text
    assert "discord" not in low
    assert "mailto:" not in low


def test_no_milestone_dates():
    text = (SITE / "index.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert not MILESTONE_DATE.search(text), "no dated milestones on an experimental product"


def test_no_emoji_on_site():
    text = (SITE / "index.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert not EMOJI.search(text)


def test_opportunity_formula_matches_core():
    core = (ROOT / "core" / "src" / "core" / "models.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert "importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)" in core  # repo truth guard
    page = (SITE / "index.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    normalized = page.lower().replace("\u2212", "-").replace(" ", "")
    assert "importance+max(importance-satisfaction,0)" in normalized


def test_404_is_self_contained():
    doc = parse("404.html")
    assert doc.lang == "en"
    assert any(lv == 1 for lv, _ in doc.headings)
    assert PAGES_URL in doc.hrefs
    assert not doc.refs, "404.html must not depend on relative assets"

+# Kiro CLI Tool Mapping
+
+Skills speak in actions ("dispatch a subagent", "create a todo", "read a file"). On the Kiro CLI these resolve to the tools below.
+
+| Action skills request | Kiro CLI equivalent |
+|---|---|
+| Invoke or load a skill | Read the skill's `SKILL.md` with the `read` tool and follow its instructions directly |
+| Create a todo / mark one complete | `todo_list` (create, add, complete, remove commands) |
+| Read a file | `read` tool (Line or Directory mode) |
+| Create or overwrite a file | `write` tool (create command) |
+| Edit a file in place | `write` tool (strReplace command) |
+| Insert content into a file | `write` tool (insert command) |
+| Delete, move, or rename a file | `shell` tool (`rm`, `mv`) |
+| Run a shell command | `shell` tool |
+| Search file contents | `grep` tool (regex pattern search) |
+| Search by symbol / semantic code search | `code` tool (search_symbols, pattern_search, etc.) |
+| Find files by name | `glob` tool |
+| List a directory | `read` tool (Directory mode) |
+| Fetch a URL | `web_fetch` tool |
+| Search the web | `web_search` tool |
+| Ask your human partner a question | Respond to the user in your message |
+| Dispatch a subagent (`Subagent (general-purpose):` template) | `subagent` tool with a `kiro_default` stage (blocking mode) |
+| Enter plan mode | `todo_list` to track steps; write designs to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` |
+| Persist progress across compaction | `todo_list` state is session-local; write ledger and briefs under `.superpowers/sdd/<plan-basename>/` (see `executing-plans`) |
+
+## Skill discovery
+
+Kiro has no automatic skill-loading tool. Skills live in `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md`. Read a skill file with the `read` tool before following it.
+
+## Subagents
+
+Kiro exposes a `subagent` tool that runs agent pipelines. Use it for the `Subagent (general-purpose):` dispatch template in skills:
+
+```json
+{
+  "task": "<overall task description>",
+  "stages": [
+    {
+      "name": "implementer",
+      "role": "kiro_default",
+      "prompt_template": "<task instructions>"
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+For `subagent-driven-development`, dispatch one implementer stage per task (blocking mode) and review its output before continuing. Parallel stages (no `depends_on`) run concurrently — use them when tasks are independent. When no parallel work is needed, dispatch stages sequentially.
+
+## Task lists / todos
+
+`todo_list` is the primary task-tracking mechanism. Use the `create` command at the start of a multi-step task, `complete` as each step finishes, and `add`/`remove` when the plan changes. `todo_list` is session-local, so also write a durable progress ledger to `.superpowers/sdd/<plan-basename>/progress.md` when running `executing-plans`.
+
+## Plan mode
+
+Kiro has no separate plan mode. Write plans to:
+
+- Designs: `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
+- Plans: `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md`
+
+Then execute them step-by-step, tracking progress with `todo_list`.
+
+## Git worktrees
+
+Kiro has no native worktree tool. Follow the `using-git-worktrees` skill Step 1b (git worktree fallback) to create worktrees manually. Check isolation first (Step 0) before creating anything.

# Agentic ODI - AI Developer Guardrails

This file provides system instructions and guardrails for any AI agents (or LLMs) assisting with the development of the **Agentic ODI** project. Please adhere to these guidelines to maintain consistency and align with the project's vision.

> **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `docs/reference/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.

---

## 🎯 ODI Methodology Guardrails

This section defines how agents MUST understand and apply Outcome-Driven Innovation within this project. These are not implementation guidelines — they are domain constraints that ensure the system reflects the ODI methodology correctly.

### What is Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)?

ODI is a strategy and innovation process rooted in the **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)** theory. Its core premise is: **people buy products and services to get a "job" done**. A "job" is the functional process a person is trying to execute — it remains stable over time, while products and technologies are point-in-time solutions that eventually become obsolete.

ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.

---

### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done

- A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
- A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
- **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
- ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.

---

### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes

- **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
- Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
- **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):

  > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`

  - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
  - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
  - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
  - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.

- **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.

---

### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)

- All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
  1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
  2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
  3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
  4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
  5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
  6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
  7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
  8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs

- **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
- ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.

---

### Stage 4: Discover Where the Market is Underserved (Opportunity Scoring)

- Each desired outcome is rated by customers on two dimensions:
  - **Importance** (1–10): How important is this outcome to the customer?
  - **Satisfaction** (1–10): How satisfied are customers with current solutions?

- **Opportunity Algorithm** (must be implemented correctly):

  ```
  Opportunity Score = Importance + Max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)
  ```

- **Interpretation**:
  - **Score > 10**: Underserved need — significant innovation opportunity.
  - **Score 10**: Appropriately served — maintain, don't over-invest.
  - **Score < 10**: Overserved — potential for disruption via lower-cost alternatives.

- **Agent rule**: Always compute and surface the opportunity score when both `importance` and `satisfaction` are provided. Highlight outcomes scoring **> 10** as the highest priority innovation targets. Use `get_outcomes(job_id)` to review the full opportunity landscape.

---

### Stage 5: Outcome-Based Market Segmentation

- ODI does **not** use demographic segmentation (age, gender, region). Instead it segments the market by **which outcomes are underserved** for each group.
- Segments can be:
  - **Underserved** — high opportunity scores, want more from existing products
  - **Overserved** — over-investing in outcomes that aren't critical; target for disruption
  - **Appropriately served** — satisfied; maintain current value

- **Agent rule**: When the user has collected outcomes with scores, help them identify outcome clusters that represent distinct market segments. This drives targeted innovation strategy.

---

### Stage 6: Formulate an Innovation Strategy

Based on the opportunity analysis, there are three strategic paths:

| Strategy | When to use |
|---|---|
| **Differentiated** | Improve existing products to address high-opportunity underserved outcomes |
| **Disruptive** | Create low-cost solutions for overserved segments that don't need all existing features |
| **New-Market** | Design products for a new job that is entirely unaddressed |

- **Agent rule**: When the opportunity landscape is clear (outcomes scored, segments identified), guide the user to select a strategy path and align their innovation roadmap accordingly.

---

### ⚠️ ODI Behavioral Guardrails for the Agent

These are absolute constraints the agent must respect:

| DO | DON'T |
|---|---|
| Always start by defining or confirming the Job-to-be-Done | Jump to solutions, features, or product ideas before the job is defined |
| Guide outcome statements with the correct format | Accept vague or solution-framed statements as valid outcomes |
| Compute opportunity scores when importance + satisfaction are available | Skip scoring or calculate it incorrectly |
| Reference the Universal Job Map when decomposing jobs | Invent arbitrary step structures disconnected from the 8 universal stages |
| Use outcome-based logic to identify market segments | Use demographics or assumptions to segment the market |
| Treat outcomes as stable, measurable success metrics | Confuse outcomes with features, preferences, or solutions |
| Call `get_odi_framework_guidelines` when stage guidance is needed | Guess at which stage comes next |

---

## 🛠 Technology Stack & Tools
- **Language**: Python 3.10+
- **MCP Framework**: `fastmcp` (Server and Client)
- **ASGI Server**: `uvicorn`
- **HTTP Client**: `httpx`
- **UI / Chat Client**: React + Vite (`apps/studio`), FastAPI sidecar (`apps/studio-api`)
- **LLM Client**: `openai` (OpenAI-compatible, used with Ollama locally)
- **Concurrency**: `asyncio`
- **Data Modeling / Validation**: `pydantic`

---

## 📄 README Maintenance Guardrail

`README.md` is the **primary human-facing entry point** for this project: a short,
high-level front door aimed at both users and developers. Detailed material lives
in `docs/` and is linked from the README. The agent MUST keep both current at all
times.

### When to update

Update the relevant file whenever any of the following change:

| Change type | Where to update |
|---|---|
| New or removed Python file / package | `README.md` **Code Overview** |
| New dependency added (`pip install ...`) | `README.md` **Quick Start → Prerequisites** |
| New way to run the project | `README.md` **Quick Start** and `docs/living-studio.md` |
| New MCP tool or capability | `README.md` **Code Overview** / relevant doc |
| New CLI command or flag | `docs/cli.md` |
| New connector kind | `docs/connectors.md` |
| New workflow or agent instruction | `docs/living-studio.md` |
| Deployment URL or cloud setup changes | `docs/deployment.md` |
| Roadmap item completed or added | `docs/roadmap.md` |
| Test layout or coverage changes | `docs/development.md` |

### Rules

- ✅ **Update docs in the same task** as the change that triggered it — never defer to a follow-up.
- ✅ **Keep README short**: it stays a high-level orientation page. Push detail into `docs/` and link to it rather than growing the README.
- ✅ **Keep the Quick Start accurate**: always reflect `uv run python scripts/dev.py` as the recommended launch command.
- ✅ **Keep Prerequisites up to date**: add any new `pip install` dependency immediately.
- ✅ **Mark Roadmap items `[x]` when completed** — do not leave stale unchecked items.
- ❌ **Never leave the README or `docs/` in a stale state** where documented commands or files no longer match the codebase.

---

## 🚧 Core Development Guardrails

### 1. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Implementation
- **Library Choice**: ALWAYS use [`fastmcp`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) for building the MCP architecture. Avoid using the lower-level Anthropic `mcp` SDK directly unless there is a hyper-specific edge case that `fastmcp` does not support.
- **Transport Protocol**: The project is currently prototyping with **HTTP transport** (not stdio). 
  - The server should be initialized using `mcp.run(transport="http", ...)`.
  - The client must connect to the HTTP endpoint (e.g., `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
- **Tool Creation**: 
  - Register tools on the server using the `@mcp.tool` decorator.
  - **CRITICAL**: Provide comprehensive docstrings and strict Python type hints for every tool parameter. Explain exactly what the tool does and what data it expects, as this metadata is fed directly to the LLM for tool discovery.
  - **Contract Synchronization**: Whenever you add, modify, or remove an MCP tool in `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`, you **MUST** simultaneously update `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` (`ToolName`, `TOOL_SPECS`) and the `get_capabilities` return string. `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` enforces the surface.

### 2. Async / Client Practices
- Use `asyncio` for client execution and IO-bound tool operations.
- Always use the `fastmcp.Client` securely within an asynchronous context manager (`async with client:`) to ensure connections are efficiently managed and closed.

### 3. Data Schema & Persistence (ODI Domain)
- Define all Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) entities (e.g., *Jobs*, *Steps*, *Desired Outcomes*, *Opportunity Scores*) using `pydantic` models.
- When expanding the server to accept complex payloads or to query data, utilize these Pydantic models for built-in type validation and schema enforcement before the server processes the request.

### 4. General Philosophy
- **Separation of Concerns**: Isolate the ODI data logic/retrieval from the MCP server tooling logic.
- **Agentic Purpose**: Remember that the tools being built are meant to be consumed by autonomous agents. Design tool interfaces that are intuitive for an LLM to call and interpret.
- **External connectors**: Integrations live in the `packages/connectors` workspace package. New kinds implement `agentic_odi_connectors.protocol.Connector` and register via `register_kind`. Do not write ingested records into `jobs_db` / outcomes unless a later mapping task says so.
- **MCP client vs ODI server**: The ODI FastMCP **server** exposes product tools. The MCP **client connector** uses `fastmcp.Client` over HTTP to ingest data from *external* MCP servers. Prefer in-memory `Client(server)` tests for that connector, same as server tests.

### 5. Testing Strategy (FastMCP)
- **First-Class Documentation**: Treat tests as living documentation that demonstrate how features work while protecting against regressions.
- **Speed & Isolation**: Tests must be fast (< 1s) and self-contained. Use `@pytest.mark.integration` or `@pytest.mark.client_process` for slower, integration, or resource-dependent tests.
- **Structure**: This repo is a uv workspace. Mirror each project's code structure in its own `tests/` directory (e.g., `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py` -> `apps/mcp-server/tests/test_server_tools.py`, `packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/mcp/connector.py` -> `packages/connectors/tests/test_mcp_connector.py`).
- **Atomic Tests**: Each test must verify exactly one specific behavior with clear intent in test names and assertions. Avoid multi-behavior tests.
- **In-Memory Testing (Preferred)**: Favor testing functionality deterministically by passing the `FastMCP` server directly into the `Client(server)` instance. This runs in-memory without network overhead for deterministic and lightning-fast execution.
- **Transport Testing (When Needed)**: For HTTP/SSE network transport tests, prefer the isolated in-process `fastmcp.utilities.tests.run_server_async(server)` context manager over subprocess testing (which uses `run_server_in_process` and is slower to debug).
- **Data Assertions**: Utilize `inline-snapshot` (`snapshot()`) for assessing complex data structures like tool API JSON schemas or expected responses.

# Development

Everything below mirrors what CI runs. Install the workspace first:

```bash
uv sync --all-packages
```

## Linting, Formatting & Type Checks

```bash
# Ruff lint and formatting checks (per-file config comes from each project's pyproject.toml)
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .

# Type checking (run per project so each project's config applies)
uv run --directory core mypy .
uv run --directory mcp_server mypy .
uv run --directory local_server mypy .
uv run --directory client mypy .
uv run --directory cli mypy .
uv run --directory connectors mypy .
uv run --directory website mypy .

# Security scanning
uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r core/src mcp_server/src local_server/src cli/src client/src connectors/src website/
```

## Frontend & Desktop Checks (studio)

The SPA and Tauri shell mirror their CI jobs locally:

```bash
npm --prefix studio run lint       # ESLint
npm --prefix studio run typecheck  # tsc --noEmit
npm --prefix studio test -- --run  # Vitest (run once)
npm --prefix studio run build      # production build → studio/dist
cd studio/src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo check
```

## Website Checks (GitHub Pages)

The `website/` static site is part of the main CI workflow. Its tests assert the
committed OG art is reproducible and that `index.html` stays in sync with the
README:

```bash
uv run --directory website pytest tests/
```

## Formatting workflow

- **When editing Python files**, either rely on the **pre-commit hooks** below
  (recommended) or run Ruff formatting directly before pushing:

  ```bash
  uv run ruff format .
  ```

- **CI behavior**:
  - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files.
  - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only.
  - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the
    changes, and push again.

## Pre-commit hooks

To run the checks automatically before each commit:

```bash
uv tool install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```

After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` run on staged files whenever you commit.
You can also trigger them manually:

```bash
pre-commit run --all-files
```

## Testing

Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely
in-memory — no running server required. Each project owns its tests:

```bash
uv run --directory core pytest
uv run --directory mcp_server pytest
uv run --directory local_server pytest
uv run --directory client pytest
uv run --directory cli pytest
uv run --directory connectors pytest
```

## Test Coverage

CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12**, combines each package's
coverage into one `coverage.xml`, and uploads it to
[Codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi) from the 3.12 job. Each
matrix job also stores its combined report as a build artifact.

The Codecov upload authenticates with the `CODECOV_TOKEN` repository secret and
is non-blocking (`fail_ci_if_error: false`), so a Codecov outage or a fork PR
without secrets cannot fail the test job. The badge at the top of the README
tracks `main`, which is the baseline every PR is compared against:

- **Project** status requires at least **90%** coverage (`target: 90%`) and
  tolerates a 1% dip from `codecov.yml`.
- **Patch** status is informational for now, so new code can land while the
  suite catches up.

To reproduce the combined report locally, run each package with its own coverage
file and merge them the way CI does:

```bash
set -e
for pkg in core mcp_server local_server client cli connectors; do
  # Absolute path, so each package writes to the repo root rather than its own directory.
  COVERAGE_FILE="$PWD/.coverage.$pkg" uv run --directory "$pkg" pytest --cov="$pkg" -q
done
uv run coverage combine .coverage.*
uv run coverage xml -o coverage.xml && uv run coverage report
```

> [!NOTE]
> Coverage is only collected for the Python packages. `studio/` and test
> directories are excluded in `codecov.yml`.

### Conventions

- Test files live under each project's `tests/` directory and are named
  `test_*.py`.
- Every async test is decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio`.
- Use `Client(mcp)` directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests.
- The server's `reset_db` autouse fixture clears in-memory state before each
  test.

# Development

Everything below mirrors what CI runs. Install the workspace first:

```bash
uv sync --all-packages
```

## Linting, Formatting & Type Checks

Shared tooling lives in the root `pyproject.toml`, so one command covers every
Python project:

```bash
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run mypy apps packages
uv run --directory website mypy .

# Security scanning
uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages website/
```

## Frontend & Desktop Checks (studio)

The SPA and Tauri shell mirror their CI jobs locally:

```bash
npm --prefix apps/studio run lint       # ESLint
npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck  # tsc --noEmit
npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run  # Vitest (run once)
npm --prefix apps/studio run build      # production build → apps/studio/dist
cd apps/studio/src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo check
```

## Website Checks (GitHub Pages)

The `website/` static site is part of the main CI workflow. Its tests assert the
committed OG art is reproducible and that `index.html` stays in sync with the
README:

```bash
uv run --directory website pytest tests/
```

## Formatting workflow

- **When editing Python files**, either rely on the **pre-commit hooks** below
  (recommended) or run Ruff formatting directly before pushing:

  ```bash
  uv run ruff format .
  ```

- **CI behavior**:
  - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files.
  - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only.
  - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the
    changes, and push again.

## Pre-commit hooks

To run the checks automatically before each commit:

```bash
uv tool install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```

After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` run on staged files whenever you commit.
You can also trigger them manually:

```bash
pre-commit run --all-files
```

## Testing

Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely
in-memory — no running server required. Tests live next to the package they
cover, and every test runs from the repository root:

```bash
uv run pytest                        # everything
uv run pytest apps/cli               # one app
uv run pytest packages/core          # one package
uv run pytest tests/contract         # cross-package contracts
uv run pytest tests/scripts          # dev launcher
```

The MCP server contract test compares the live FastMCP registry with
`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py`, so add or change a tool in
both places. The CLI local-backend contract test keeps `_LOCAL_HANDLERS` aligned
with the same tool names.

## Test Coverage

CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and uploads one combined
`coverage.xml` from the 3.12 job to
[Codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi).

The Codecov upload authenticates with the `CODECOV_TOKEN` repository secret and
is non-blocking (`fail_ci_if_error: false`), so a Codecov outage or a fork PR
without secrets cannot fail the test job. The badge at the top of the README
tracks `main`, which is the baseline every PR is compared against:

- **Project** status requires at least **90%** coverage (`target: 90%`) and
  tolerates a 1% dip from `codecov.yml`.
- **Patch** status is informational for now, so new code can land while the
  suite catches up.

To reproduce the report locally:

```bash
uv run pytest \
  --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
  --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
  --cov=agentic_odi_core \
  --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
  --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
  --cov-report=term-missing \
  --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml
```

> [!NOTE]
> Coverage is only collected for the Python packages. `apps/studio/` and test
> directories are excluded in `codecov.yml`.

### Conventions

- Test files live under each project's `tests/` directory and are named
  `test_*.py`.
- Root `tests/` is reserved for cross-package checks (`contract/` and
  `scripts/`).
- Every async test is decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio`.
- Use `Client(mcp)` directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests.
- The MCP server's `reset_db` autouse fixture clears in-memory state before
  each test.

### Test Coverage Map

| Area | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `packages/core/tests/` | Domain models, opportunity scoring, `ODIService`, repository implementations, SQLite persistence, schema, and repository factory |
| `apps/mcp-server/tests/` | Full ODI workflow, entity parity, context tools, Customer Outcomes, evidence, tool errors, and HTTP transport startup |
| `apps/studio-api/tests/` | Health, config, canvas, SSE chat, SPA fallback, MCP hydration, probes, and step/outcome passthrough |
| `apps/cli/tests/` | Backend selection, local/remote CRUD, chat, wizard, onboarding, updates, rendering, connectors, and startup performance |
| `packages/connectors/tests/` | Catalog presets, registry persistence, factory, MCP and REST connectors, evidence mapping, and sink |
| `tests/contract/` | Live MCP tool surface and CLI local-handler parity |
| `tests/scripts/` | `scripts/dev.py` startup, port checks, signals, and shutdown |
| `apps/studio/src/**/*.test.ts` | SPA units: ODI math, transport bridge, SSE parser, sidecar client |
| `website/tests/` | Static site integrity, OG art reproducibility, and README sync |

> [!TIP]
> Type `/test` in the AI assistant to have the agent run all tests and report the
> results automatically.

## Agent Session Tracking

Agent sessions are captured with the [Entire](https://docs.entire.io/overview)
CLI. The repository integration lives in `.entire/settings.json`,
`.cursor/hooks.json`, and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. Run `entire status` to
confirm it is enabled and `entire checkpoint list` to inspect captured
checkpoints.

# Data Flow

## Sources of Truth

| Layer | Owns | Persists |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/core` | `Job`, `Step`, `Outcome`, `CustomerOutcome`, `ODIService`, repository protocol | SQLite event log + snapshots |
| `apps/mcp-server` | MCP tool adapters over `ODIService` | Via the repository chosen in `configure(repo)`; SQLite in production |
| `apps/studio-api` | Studio API, canvas projection, chat tool loop | Via the same repository when the local backend is active |
| `apps/studio` | Presentation state, optimistic canvas updates | Browser cache only |
| `apps/cli` | Terminal rendering, local/remote backend selection | SQLite directly for `local`, no local writes for `mcp` |

## Write Paths

### Local CLI

```text
agentic-odi customer-outcomes add
  -> LocalBackend
  -> ODIService
  -> SQLiteRepository
  -> IntentStore (append) + snapshot refresh
```

### MCP

```text
MCP client / Studio MCP mode / CLI --backend mcp
  -> FastMCP tool
  -> ODIService
  -> configured Repository
```

`apps/mcp-server` starts with an in-memory repository for tests. `main()` calls `configure(SQLiteRepository())` before `mcp.run(...)`, so the network server always persists.

### Studio API

```text
apps/studio SPA
  -> /api/canvas, /api/steps, /api/outcomes
  -> backend=local: ODIService -> Repository
  -> backend=mcp:   call_mcp_tool -> MCP server -> ODIService -> Repository

apps/studio SPA
  -> /api/chat
  -> stream_chat -> OpenAI-compatible LLM -> MCP tool calls
```

The SPA sends `mcp_url` with every data request for compatibility. In `local` mode the sidecar ignores it; in `mcp` mode it is required for canvas and mutations.

## Read Paths

```text
ODIService.get_jobs / get_job_map / get_outcomes
  -> Repository read-through state
  -> Pydantic models
  -> JSON (CLI --json, MCP text payload, Studio canvas)
```

The Studio canvas falls back to the demo seed only in `mcp` mode when MCP is unreachable or returns no jobs. `local` mode returns exactly what is in the local database, including an empty canvas.

## Configuration

| Variable | Used by | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | core SQLite repository | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | CLI, Studio API | `local` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | CLI, Studio defaults | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DIST` | Studio API, dev launcher | `apps/apps/studio/dist` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT` | Tauri shell | auto-detected |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `http://localhost:8001/v1` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `local-tools-model` |
| `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `local` |

## Trust Boundaries

- The SPA runs in a browser or Tauri webview and only trusts the sidecar origin.
- The sidecar may reach MCP and the LLM; CORS is restricted to known Studio origins.
- MCP is an HTTP service with no authentication in local development. Do not expose it directly to the internet; the Cloudflare setup tunnels the sidecar, not MCP.
===
# Repository Architecture

Agentic ODI is a uv workspace with a single root `pyproject.toml` for shared tooling. Python distributions are imported by their stable `agentic_odi_*` package names; directory layout does not leak into imports.

## Layout

```text
apps/
  cli/            agentic_odi_cli         Typer CLI: local SQLite or remote MCP
  mcp-server/     agentic_odi_mcp_server  FastMCP server over HTTP
  studio-api/     agentic_odi_studio_api  FastAPI sidecar for the Studio SPA
  studio/         React + TypeScript + Vite SPA and Tauri 2 shell
packages/
  core/           agentic_odi_core        Domain, services, repositories, contract
  connectors/     agentic_odi_connectors  MCP client connectors and catalog
infra/cloudflare/ Worker + Wrangler config for the free-plan deployment
scripts/          Dev launcher, binary build, installer checks
tests/            Cross-package contract and launcher tests only
docs/             Architecture, reference material, Superpowers artifacts
packaging/        PyInstaller spec for the CLI binary
```

## Dependency Direction

```text
apps/cli ──────────────┐
apps/mcp-server ───────┼──▶ packages/core
apps/studio-api ───────┘         ▲
                                 │
apps/cli ──────────────▶ packages/connectors
```

- `packages/core` depends on no other workspace package.
- `packages/connectors` depends on `core` only where it needs shared models.
- Every runnable app may depend on `core`; none of them imports another app.
- The React SPA only talks to `apps/studio-api` over `/api`; it never calls MCP or the LLM directly.

## Persistence

- `SQLiteRepository` is the production default for the CLI, MCP server, and Studio API.
- The default database is `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_DB`.
- `InMemoryRepository` is the default inside tests and for the module-level MCP server before `configure(repo)` runs.
- The CLI selects its backend with `--backend local|mcp` or `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND`.
- The Studio API selects `local` (direct service calls) or `mcp` (passthrough) with `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` or `create_app(backend=...)`.

## MCP Contract

`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` owns `ToolName`, `ToolSpec`, `TOOL_SPECS`, and `TOOL_NAMES`. The live FastMCP registry is asserted against it by `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py`; the CLI's local handlers are checked by `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py`.

## Entry Points

| Command | Module |
|---|---|
| `agentic-odi` | `agentic_odi_cli.cli:app` |
| `agentic-odi-server` / `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | `agentic_odi_mcp_server.mcp_server:main` |
| `agentic-odi-studio-api` | `agentic_odi_studio_api.main:main` |
| `uv run python scripts/dev.py` | Dev launcher (MCP + Studio API) |

## Related

- [Data flow](data-flow.md)
- [Testing](testing.md)
===
# Testing

## Commands

```bash
uv run pytest                       # all packages + root contract/launcher tests
uv run pytest packages/core         # one package
uv run pytest tests/contract        # MCP contract only
uv run mypy apps packages tests
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages
```

The root `pyproject.toml` owns pytest, coverage, ruff, mypy, and bandit configuration. There is no per-package test configuration to keep in sync.

## Layout

Tests live next to their package (`packages/*/tests`, `apps/*/tests`). Root `tests/` contains only cross-package checks:

- `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` — live FastMCP names, argument names, and required fields match `agentic_odi_core.contract.TOOL_SPECS`.
- `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py` — the CLI local-handler keys are a subset of `TOOL_NAMES`.
- `tests/scripts/` — dev launcher helpers and lifecycle.

## Isolation Rules

- Use `InMemoryRepository` in tests. `create_app(InMemoryRepository())` keeps the Studio API off the real `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`.
- The MCP server module starts in-memory; tests call tools through `Client(mcp)` without HTTP.
- `configure(repo)` swaps the server's service and repository. Production calls it once in `main()`; tests should call it only when they intend to replace state.
- Async tests use `@pytest.mark.asyncio` (strict mode).

## Coverage

CI runs the root suite on Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12, collects coverage for every `agentic_odi_*` distribution, and uploads `coverage.xml` from the 3.12 job. Codecov requires 90% project coverage; patch coverage is advisory. Python tests and `apps/studio/**` are excluded from the report by `codecov.yml`.

## Frontend

```bash
npm --prefix apps/studio run lint
npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck
npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run
npm --prefix apps/studio run build
cd apps/apps/studio/src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo check
```

# Running The Living Studio

**The Living Studio** is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation:
an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact
Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent
connected to the MCP server.

The Studio runs three ways. All of them serve the same SPA, which talks only to
the sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:8100` — the SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM
directly.

## Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────────┐  /api (JSON)  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
│  Living Studio SPA         │ ────────────▶ │  local_server (sidecar)       │
│  React + TS + Vite         │  /api/chat    │  FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100    │
│  (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │  - config / health / canvas   │
└────────────────────────────┘  SSE stream   │  - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │
                                             │  - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop)  │
                                             └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                             │ MCP (HTTP)
                                                             ▼
                                             ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                             │  mcp_server  :8000/mcp        │
                                             └───────────────────────────────┘
                                                             ▲
                                                             │ OpenAI-compatible
                                             ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                                             │  Your local LLM backend       │
                                             └───────────────────────────────┘
```

## 1. Web — production build (recommended for a quick look)

```bash
npm --prefix apps/studio run build   # build the SPA into apps/studio/dist
python scripts/dev.py            # starts MCP :8000 + sidecar :8100
```

| Service | URL |
|---|---|
| MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp |
| Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 |

`python scripts/dev.py` starts both processes concurrently; press **Ctrl+C** to
stop both.

## 2. Web — dev with hot reload

Vite proxies `/api` to the sidecar:

```bash
npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full   # MCP + sidecar + Vite together
# open http://localhost:5173
```

## 3. Desktop — Tauri 2

The app spawns the MCP server and sidecar itself:

```bash
npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev     # dev window
npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri build   # bundles: .deb / .AppImage (Linux), .app / .dmg (macOS), .msi / .exe (Windows)
```

> [!NOTE]
> **Tauri prerequisites.** The desktop build needs the WebKitGTK toolchain and
> Rust 1.90+. On Debian/Ubuntu:
>
> ```bash
> sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential pkg-config curl wget file \
>   libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf xdg-utils libfuse2t64
> ```
>
> The Tauri CLI ships as the `@tauri-apps/cli` npm dev dependency
> (`npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri`). The sidecar is launched with
> `uv run python -m …` from the repository root; if the app cannot locate the
> repo root, set `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT`.

## Desktop signing & updater secrets

Self-updating and code signing are **env-driven**: if a secret is absent, an
unsigned artifact is produced instead of failing. CI reads these from GitHub
Actions secrets.

| Secret | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | Signs updater artifacts (`.sig`) and the `latest.json` manifest. A tagged release fails loudly without it. Generate with `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate`. |
| `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | Password for the private key (optional when the key has none). |
| `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` / `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | macOS Developer ID certificate (base64 `.p12`) and its password. |
| `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` | macOS signing identity. |
| `APPLE_ID` / `APPLE_PASSWORD` / `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | macOS notarization credentials. |
| `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE` / `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | Windows Authenticode PFX (base64) and its password; imported by CI and injected into the bundle config. |

Releases are published by `.github/workflows/tauri-release.yml` when a `v*` tag
is pushed. The desktop app checks for updates on startup and via
**Settings → Check for updates**.

### Managing the updater signing key

The updater key pair authenticates release artifacts so an installed app can
verify that an auto-update genuinely came from you. The **public** key is
embedded in `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (`plugins.updater.pubkey`) and is
safe to commit. The **private** key must never be committed, logged, printed in
CI, or attached to a build artifact.

1. **Generate a key pair** (only if you need a new one). Leave `-p ""` for a
   passwordless key, or pass a password and remember it:

   ```bash
   npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate -- -w ./living-studio.key -p "" -f
   ```

   This writes `living-studio.key` (private, `0600`) and `living-studio.key.pub`
   (public).

2. **Paste the public key** into `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`:

   ```jsonc
   {
     "plugins": {
       "updater": {
         "endpoints": ["https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/latest.json"],
         "pubkey": "<contents of living-studio.key.pub>"
       }
     }
   }
   ```

3. **Store the private key outside the repository** (the repo root is
   git-tracked; a sibling directory is not), with restricted permissions:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys && chmod 700 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys
   mv living-studio.key ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/
   chmod 600 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
   ```

   Move it to a long-term secret store (password manager, 1Password/Bitwarden/
   Vault, or a private encrypted backup) when you decide where that lives.
   Losing it means future releases can no longer be signed for existing
   installs.

4. **Add the private key as a GitHub Actions secret** (Settings → Secrets and
   variables → Actions → New repository secret), or via the CLI:

   ```bash
   gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
   gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD --body ""   # only if you set a password
   ```

5. **Verify** the secrets exist (values are never displayed):

   ```bash
   gh secret list
   ```

6. **Rotate** by repeating steps 1–4, then publishing a release signed with the
   new key. Existing installs still verify against the public key compiled into
   their binary, so keep the old private key usable and publish the new public
   key ahead of the cut-over.

> [!CAUTION]
> If the private key leaks, treat auto-updates as compromised: generate a new
> pair, rotate the Actions secret, and publish a freshly signed release.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Migration note.** The Streamlit UI (`apps/studio/src/App.tsx`) has been
> removed. The Living Studio now lives in `studio/` (browser SPA + Tauri desktop
> app) and is served by the `local_server` sidecar on port **8100** (previously
> Streamlit's `8501`). Start everything with `python scripts/dev.py`. All
> `AGENTIC_ODI_*` environment variable names, the demo dataset, and the ODI
> formulas are unchanged.

## Connecting an LLM

The Studio needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM backend with tool-calling support to
drive the agent. For a fully local setup, see
[Local LLM Backend](local-llm.md).

## Agent-Driven Testing

Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it starts
both processes, opens the browser, sends a test message, and reports the results.

Type `/test` to have the agent run all tests and report the results
automatically.

import signal
import socket

        return s.connect_ex(("localhost", port)) == 0

    """Return the (mcp_server, sidecar) argv lists, both shell-free and fixed."""

        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, *exc: Any) -> bool:
        return False

    async def call_tool(self, name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        self.calls.append((name, arguments))

 def _startup_auto_update(no_update: bool) -> None:
     """Best-effort background auto-update; never raises, never blocks."""
     try:

         if updated is not None:

     ),

 def _reexec_current() -> None:
     """Re-exec into the freshly installed binary (POSIX only)."""
     current = paths.current_link()
     binary = current / "odi"
     can_exec = (
         os.name == "posix" and hasattr(os, "execv") and current.is_symlink() and binary.exists()
     )
     if not can_exec:
         typer.echo("Update applied; it will take effect on the next run.")
         return
     argv = sys.argv[1:]
     if "update" in argv:
         argv = argv[: argv.index("update")]
     os.execv(str(binary), [str(binary), *argv])  # nosec B606 - re-execs own verified binary
 
 
 @app.command(name="schema")
 def schema_cmd() -> None:
     """Print the canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity."""
     typer.echo(json.dumps(run_tool("get_odi_schema", {}), indent=2))
 
 
 @app.command(name="version")
 def version_cmd() -> None:
     """Show CLI version."""
     typer.echo(version.build_summary())
 
 
 @app.command(name="update")
 def update_cmd(
     check: bool = False,
     force: bool = False,
     version: str | None = None,
     now: bool = False,
 ) -> None:
     """Check for or apply CLI updates."""
     if check:
         latest = update.latest_release(__version__)
         if latest is None:
             typer.echo(f"Already up to date (v{__version__}).")
         else:
             typer.echo(f"Update available: v{latest} - run 'odi update' to install.")
         return
 
     if not paths.is_frozen():
         typer.echo("This is a source install; use your package manager to update.")
         return
 
     target = version.lstrip("v") if version else update.latest_release(__version__)
     if target is None:
         if force:
             target = __version__
         else:
             typer.echo(f"Already up to date (v{__version__}).")
             return
 
     try:
         with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="odi-update-") as tmp:
             archive = update.download(target, Path(tmp))
             digest = hashlib.sha256(archive.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
             update.perform_update(target, archive, digest, paths.install_root())
     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
         typer.echo(f"Update failed: {exc}", err=True)
         raise typer.Exit(code=1) from exc
 
     typer.echo(f"Updated to v{target}")
     if now:
         _reexec_current()
 
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     app()
