 # Deployment
 
 The server is deployed via **[Horizon Prefect](https://www.prefect.io/horizon)**,
 Prefect's managed infrastructure for hosting MCP-compatible agents.
 
 ## Test Chat (UI)
 
 Interact with the deployed agent directly in your browser:
 
 > **[https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat](https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat)**
 
 ## MCP Server Endpoint
 
 Integrate via the MCP protocol at:
 
 > **[https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp](https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp)**
 
 > [!IMPORTANT]
 > **Authentication is required** to access the MCP server endpoint. Please reach
 > out to the maintainers to obtain the necessary credentials before connecting a
 > client.
 
 ## Living Studio on a Free Cloudflare Worker
 
 Workers Containers — the only way to run the Python sidecar entirely on
 Cloudflare — requires the Workers Paid plan. On the free plan, the Worker serves
 the built SPA as Workers Static Assets and proxies `/api/*` to the sidecar
 through a free, account-less
 [Cloudflare Quick Tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/get-started/quick-tunnels/).
 
 `wrangler.jsonc` publishes `apps/studio/dist` with SPA fallback and runs the Worker
-first for `/api/*`; `cloudflare/worker.ts` forwards those calls to the
+first for `/api/*`; `infra/cloudflare/worker.ts` forwards those calls to the
 `SIDECAR_URL` secret. The browser only talks to the Worker origin, so the
 sidecar's CORS list is not involved.
 
 ```bash
 # 1. Build the SPA that the Worker uploads as static assets
 npm --prefix apps/studio ci
 npm --prefix apps/studio run build
 
 # 2. Terminal A — MCP server (:8000) + sidecar (:8100)
 python scripts/dev.py
 
 # 3. Terminal B — free public URL for the sidecar (no account required)
 cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8100
 # copy the https://<random>.trycloudflare.com URL it prints
 
 # 4. Store the URL on the Worker, then deploy
 npx wrangler secret put SIDECAR_URL   # paste the trycloudflare URL
 npx wrangler deploy
 ```
 
 Workers Builds settings (Workers & Pages → your Worker → Settings → Builds):
 
 | Setting | Value |
 |---|---|
 | Root directory | `/` |
 | Build command | `npm --prefix apps/studio ci && npm --prefix apps/studio run build` |
 | Deploy command | `npx wrangler deploy` |
 
 A Worker has no run command: the Worker script runs on Cloudflare. Set `name` in
 `wrangler.jsonc` to the Worker you created before the first deploy.
 
 > [!NOTE]
 > The sidecar runs on your machine, so the Worker only works while
 > `python scripts/dev.py` and the Quick Tunnel are running. Quick Tunnel URLs
 > change on every restart — update the secret with
 > `npx wrangler secret put SIDECAR_URL`. Chat also needs a reachable
 > OpenAI-compatible endpoint in the Studio's **Settings**; the canvas, job map,
 > and impact simulation work without one.

 # Running The Living Studio
 
 **The Living Studio** is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation:
 an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact
 Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent
 connected to the MCP server.
 
 The Studio runs three ways. All of them serve the same SPA, which talks only to
 the sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:8100` — the SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM
 directly.
 
 ## Architecture
 
 ```text
 ┌────────────────────────────┐  /api (JSON)  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
-│  Living Studio SPA         │ ────────────▶ │  apps/studio-api (sidecar)       │
+│  Living Studio SPA         │ ────────────▶ │  apps/studio-api (sidecar)    │
 │  React + TS + Vite         │  /api/chat    │  FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100    │
 │  (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │  - config / health / canvas   │
 └────────────────────────────┘  SSE stream   │  - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │
                                              │  - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop)  │
                                              └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                              │ MCP (HTTP)
                                                              ▼
                                              ┌───────────────────────────────┐
-                                             │  apps/mcp-server :8000/mcp        │
+                                             │  apps/mcp-server :8000/mcp    │
                                              └───────────────────────────────┘
                                                              ▲
                                                              │ OpenAI-compatible
                                              ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                                              │  Your local LLM backend       │
                                              └───────────────────────────────┘
 ```
 
 ## 1. Web — production build (recommended for a quick look)
 
 ```bash
 npm --prefix apps/studio run build   # build the SPA into apps/studio/dist
 python scripts/dev.py            # starts MCP :8000 + sidecar :8100
 ```
 
 | Service | URL |
 |---|---|
 | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp |
 | Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 |
 
 `python scripts/dev.py` starts both processes concurrently; press **Ctrl+C** to
 stop both.
 
 ## 2. Web — dev with hot reload
 
 Vite proxies `/api` to the sidecar:
 
 ```bash
 npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full   # MCP + sidecar + Vite together
 # open http://localhost:5173
 ```
 
 ## 3. Desktop — Tauri 2
 
 The app spawns the MCP server and sidecar itself:
 
 ```bash
 npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev     # dev window
 npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri build   # bundles: .deb / .AppImage (Linux), .app / .dmg (macOS), .msi / .exe (Windows)
 ```
 
 > [!NOTE]
 > **Tauri prerequisites.** The desktop build needs the WebKitGTK toolchain and
 > Rust 1.90+. On Debian/Ubuntu:
 >
 > ```bash
 > sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential pkg-config curl wget file \
 >   libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf xdg-utils libfuse2t64
 > ```
 >
 > The Tauri CLI ships as the `@tauri-apps/cli` npm dev dependency
 > (`npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri`). The sidecar is launched with
 > `uv run python -m …` from the repository root; if the app cannot locate the
 > repo root, set `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT`.
 
 ## Desktop signing & updater secrets
 
 Self-updating and code signing are **env-driven**: if a secret is absent, an
 unsigned artifact is produced instead of failing. CI reads these from GitHub
 Actions secrets.
 
 | Secret | Purpose |
 |---|---|
 | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | Signs updater artifacts (`.sig`) and the `latest.json` manifest. A tagged release fails loudly without it. Generate with `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate`. |
 | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | Password for the private key (optional when the key has none). |
 | `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` / `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | macOS Developer ID certificate (base64 `.p12`) and its password. |
 | `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` | macOS signing identity. |
 | `APPLE_ID` / `APPLE_PASSWORD` / `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | macOS notarization credentials. |
 | `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE` / `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | Windows Authenticode PFX (base64) and its password; imported by CI and injected into the bundle config. |
 
 Releases are published by `.github/workflows/tauri-release.yml` when a `v*` tag
 is pushed. The desktop app checks for updates on startup and via
 **Settings → Check for updates**.
 
 ### Managing the updater signing key
 
 The updater key pair authenticates release artifacts so an installed app can
 verify that an auto-update genuinely came from you. The **public** key is
 embedded in `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (`plugins.updater.pubkey`) and is
 safe to commit. The **private** key must never be committed, logged, printed in
 CI, or attached to a build artifact.
 
 1. **Generate a key pair** (only if you need a new one). Leave `-p ""` for a
    passwordless key, or pass a password and remember it:
 
    ```bash
    npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate -- -w ./living-studio.key -p "" -f
    ```
 
    This writes `living-studio.key` (private, `0600`) and `living-studio.key.pub`
    (public).
 
 2. **Paste the public key** into `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`:
 
    ```jsonc
    {
      "plugins": {
        "updater": {
          "endpoints": ["https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/latest.json"],
          "pubkey": "<contents of living-studio.key.pub>"
        }
      }
    }
    ```
 
 3. **Store the private key outside the repository** (the repo root is
    git-tracked; a sibling directory is not), with restricted permissions:
 
    ```bash
    mkdir -p ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys && chmod 700 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys
    mv living-studio.key ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/
    chmod 600 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
    ```
 
    Move it to a long-term secret store (password manager, 1Password/Bitwarden/
    Vault, or a private encrypted backup) when you decide where that lives.
    Losing it means future releases can no longer be signed for existing
    installs.
 
 4. **Add the private key as a GitHub Actions secret** (Settings → Secrets and
    variables → Actions → New repository secret), or via the CLI:
 
    ```bash
    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD --body ""   # only if you set a password
    ```
 
 5. **Verify** the secrets exist (values are never displayed):
 
    ```bash
    gh secret list
    ```
 
 6. **Rotate** by repeating steps 1–4, then publishing a release signed with the
    new key. Existing installs still verify against the public key compiled into
    their binary, so keep the old private key usable and publish the new public
    key ahead of the cut-over.
 
 > [!CAUTION]
 > If the private key leaks, treat auto-updates as compromised: generate a new
 > pair, rotate the Actions secret, and publish a freshly signed release.
 
 > [!IMPORTANT]
 > **Migration note.** The Streamlit UI has been removed. The Living Studio now
 > lives in `apps/studio/` (browser SPA + Tauri desktop app) and is served by the
 > `apps/studio-api` sidecar on port **8100** (previously Streamlit's `8501`).
 > Start everything with `python scripts/dev.py`. All `AGENTIC_ODI_*` environment
 > variable names, the demo dataset, and the ODI formulas are unchanged.

# Deployment

The server is deployed via **[Horizon Prefect](https://www.prefect.io/horizon)**,
Prefect's managed infrastructure for hosting MCP-compatible agents.

## Test Chat (UI)

Interact with the deployed agent directly in your browser:

> **[https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat](https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat)**

## MCP Server Endpoint

Integrate via the MCP protocol at:

> **[https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp](https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp)**

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Authentication is required** to access the MCP server endpoint. Please reach
> out to the maintainers to obtain the necessary credentials before connecting a
> client.

## Living Studio on a Free Cloudflare Worker

Workers Containers — the only way to run the Python sidecar entirely on
Cloudflare — requires the Workers Paid plan. On the free plan, the Worker serves
the built SPA as Workers Static Assets and proxies `/api/*` to the sidecar
through a free, account-less
[Cloudflare Quick Tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/get-started/quick-tunnels/).

`wrangler.jsonc` publishes `apps/studio/dist` with SPA fallback and runs the Worker
first for `/api/*`; `cloudflare/worker.ts` forwards those calls to the
`SIDECAR_URL` secret. The browser only talks to the Worker origin, so the
sidecar's CORS list is not involved.

```bash
# 1. Build the SPA that the Worker uploads as static assets
npm --prefix apps/studio ci
npm --prefix apps/studio run build

# 2. Terminal A — MCP server (:8000) + sidecar (:8100)
python scripts/dev.py

# 3. Terminal B — free public URL for the sidecar (no account required)
cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8100
# copy the https://<random>.trycloudflare.com URL it prints

# 4. Store the URL on the Worker, then deploy
npx wrangler secret put SIDECAR_URL   # paste the trycloudflare URL
npx wrangler deploy
```

Workers Builds settings (Workers & Pages → your Worker → Settings → Builds):

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Root directory | `/` |
| Build command | `npm --prefix apps/studio ci && npm --prefix apps/studio run build` |
| Deploy command | `npx wrangler deploy` |

A Worker has no run command: the Worker script runs on Cloudflare. Set `name` in
`wrangler.jsonc` to the Worker you created before the first deploy.

> [!NOTE]
> The sidecar runs on your machine, so the Worker only works while
> `python scripts/dev.py` and the Quick Tunnel are running. Quick Tunnel URLs
> change on every restart — update the secret with
> `npx wrangler secret put SIDECAR_URL`. Chat also needs a reachable
> OpenAI-compatible endpoint in the Studio's **Settings**; the canvas, job map,
> and impact simulation work without one.

state.output:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Ruff Lint (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff check .

      - name: Verify Ruff Formatting (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Mypy
        run: uv run mypy apps packages

      - name: Run Mypy (website)
        run: uv run --directory website mypy .

  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Bandit
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages

      - name: Run Bandit (website)
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r website/

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Pytest
        run: |
          uv run pytest \
            --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
            --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
            --cov=agentic_odi_core \
            --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
            --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
            --cov-report=term-missing \
            --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml

      - name: Upload coverage report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: coverage.xml
          if-no-files-found: error

      # One upload per run is enough; the 3.12 report is the canonical one.
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ matrix.python-version == '3.12' }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: coverage.xml
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: CLI reports a version
        run: |
          version="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli --version)"
          [ -n "$version" ]
          echo "OK: $version"

      - name: CLI exposes connectors commands
        run: |
          help="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors --help)"
          echo "$help" | grep -q list
          echo "$help" | grep -q ingest
          echo "OK: connectors help"

      - name: Installer installs from a simulated release
        run: bash scripts/tests/install_e2e.sh

      - name: MCP server boots and serves /mcp
        run: |
          uv run python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server > /tmp/mcp_server.log 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sfX POST http://localhost:8000/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
              -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "MCP server did not respond on :8000/mcp"
            cat /tmp/mcp_server.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: MCP server responded with 200"

      - name: Living Studio sidecar serves the studio API
        run: |
          AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND=mcp uv run python -m agentic_odi_studio_api.main > /tmp/sidecar.log 2>&1 &
          SIDECAR_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/health/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"mcp_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp"}' -o /dev/null &&
              curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/canvas?mcp_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp" -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "Living Studio sidecar did not respond on :8100"
            cat /tmp/sidecar.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: sidecar studio API responded with 200"

      - name: scripts/dev.py brings up both services and stops cleanly
        run: |
          uv run python scripts/dev.py > /tmp/clientrun.log 2>&1 &
          RUN_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/config &&
              curl -sfX POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp \
                -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
                -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "scripts/dev.py did not bring up both services"
            cat /tmp/clientrun.log
            kill "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 1
          fi
          kill -INT "$RUN_PID"
          wait "$RUN_PID"
          echo "OK: both services stopped cleanly"

  website:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Pytest (website)
        run: uv run --directory website pytest tests/

      - name: Build site (rsync)
        run: |
          mkdir -p _site
          rsync -av website/ _site/ --exclude='tests/' --exclude='tools/'

  studio:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Ruff Lint (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff check .

      - name: Verify Ruff Formatting (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Mypy
        run: uv run mypy apps packages

      - name: Run Mypy (website)
        run: uv run --directory website mypy .

  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Bandit
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages

      - name: Run Bandit (website)
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r website/

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Pytest
        run: |
          uv run pytest \
            --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
            --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
            --cov=agentic_odi_core \
            --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
            --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
            --cov-report=term-missing \
            --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml

      - name: Upload coverage report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: coverage.xml
          if-no-files-found: error

      # One upload per run is enough; the 3.12 report is the canonical one.
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ matrix.python-version == '3.12' }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: coverage.xml
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: CLI reports a version
        run: |
          version="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli --version)"
          [ -n "$version" ]
          echo "OK: $version"

      - name: CLI exposes connectors commands
        run: |
          help="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors --help)"
          echo "$help" | grep -q list
          echo "$help" | grep -q ingest
          echo "OK: connectors help"

      - name: Installer installs from a simulated release
        run: bash scripts/tests/install_e2e.sh

      - name: MCP server boots and serves /mcp
        run: |
          uv run python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server > /tmp/mcp_server.log 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sfX POST http://localhost:8000/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
              -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "MCP server did not respond on :8000/mcp"
            cat /tmp/mcp_server.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: MCP server responded with 200"

      - name: Living Studio sidecar serves the studio API
        run: |
          AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND=mcp uv run python -m agentic_odi_studio_api.main > /tmp/sidecar.log 2>&1 &
          SIDECAR_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/health/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"mcp_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp"}' -o /dev/null &&
              curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/canvas?mcp_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp" -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "Living Studio sidecar did not respond on :8100"
            cat /tmp/sidecar.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: sidecar studio API responded with 200"

      - name: scripts/dev.py brings up both services and stops cleanly
        run: |
          uv run python scripts/dev.py > /tmp/clientrun.log 2>&1 &
          RUN_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/config &&
              curl -sfX POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp \
                -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
                -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "scripts/dev.py did not bring up both services"
            cat /tmp/clientrun.log
            kill "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 1
          fi
          kill -INT "$RUN_PID"
          wait "$RUN_PID"
          echo "OK: both services stopped cleanly"

  website:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Pytest (website)
        run: uv run --directory website pytest tests/

      - name: Build site (rsync)
        run: |
          mkdir -p _site
          rsync -av website/ _site/ --exclude='tests/' --exclude='tools/'

  studio:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio

  tauri-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio/src-tauri
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Cargo fmt
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: Cargo clippy
        run: cargo clippy -- -D warnings

      - name: Cargo check
        run: cargo check

  tauri-build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: npm ci
        working-directory: apps/studio

      - name: Configure updater artifacts
        working-directory: apps/studio
        env:
          SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo 'TAURI_CONFIG={"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}' >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "No TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY provided — building without signed updater artifacts."
          fi

      - name: Build desktop bundle
        working-directory: apps/studio
        env:
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: npm run tauri build

      - name: Upload desktop bundles
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: tauri-bundles-linux
          if-no-files-found: warn
          path: |
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/*.deb
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage.sig

  ci-green:
    name: CI green
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test, smoke, website, studio, tauri-check, tauri-build]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Verify all required jobs succeeded
        run: |
          results='${{ join(needs.*.result, ' ') }}'
          echo "Job results: $results"
          for result in $results; do
            if [ "$result" != "success" ]; then
              echo "::error::A required job did not succeed ($results)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "OK: all required jobs succeeded"

"""
run.py — Local dev launcher for Agentic ODI.

Starts the FastMCP server (``python -m mcp_server``) and the Living Studio
sidecar (``uvicorn local_server.app:create_app --factory``) concurrently, then
prints the MCP and Studio URLs. Shutting down this script (Ctrl+C) terminates
both processes.

Usage:
    python -m client.run
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import signal
import socket
import subprocess  # nosec B404 - launches only fixed child commands (see B603 notes)
import sys
import time

MCP_PORT = 8000
STUDIO_PORT = 8100

REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(
    os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
)
SPA_DIST = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "studio", "dist")
SPA_BUILD_HINT = "Frontend not built — run `npm --prefix studio run build` to serve the Studio UI."


def is_port_in_use(port: int) -> bool:
    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
        return s.connect_ex(("localhost", port)) == 0


def build_commands() -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    """Return the (mcp_server, sidecar) argv lists, both shell-free and fixed."""
    mcp_command = [sys.executable, "-m", "mcp_server"]
    sidecar_command = [
        sys.executable,
        "-m",
        "uvicorn",
        "local_server.app:create_app",
        "--factory",
        "--host",
        "127.0.0.1",
        "--port",
        str(STUDIO_PORT),
    ]
    return mcp_command, sidecar_command


def start_server() -> subprocess.Popen:
    if is_port_in_use(MCP_PORT):
        print(f"Error: Port {MCP_PORT} is already in use.")
        print("Please stop any process running on this port and try again.")
        sys.exit(1)

    mcp_command, _ = build_commands()
    print(f"Starting MCP server on http://localhost:{MCP_PORT}/mcp ...")
    # Fixed command, no shell, no untrusted input.
    return subprocess.Popen(mcp_command)  # nosec B603


def start_studio() -> subprocess.Popen:
    if is_port_in_use(STUDIO_PORT):
        print(f"Warning: Port {STUDIO_PORT} is already in use. The sidecar may fail to start.")

    _, sidecar_command = build_commands()
    print(f"Starting Living Studio sidecar on http://localhost:{STUDIO_PORT} ...")
    # Fixed command, no shell, no untrusted input.
    return subprocess.Popen(sidecar_command)  # nosec B603


def main() -> None:
    server = None
    studio = None

    def shutdown(signum=None, frame=None):
        print("\nShutting down...")
        if studio:
            studio.terminate()
        if server:
            server.terminate()

        try:
            if studio:
                studio.wait(timeout=5)
            if server:
                server.wait(timeout=5)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:

        print("✅ All processes stopped.")
        sys.exit(0)

    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, shutdown)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, shutdown)

    try:
        server = start_server()
        # Give the server a moment to bind its port before the sidecar connects
        time.sleep(2)
        studio = start_studio()

        print("\nBoth processes are running.")
        print(f"MCP Server   -> http://localhost:{MCP_PORT}/mcp")
        print(f"Living Studio -> http://localhost:{STUDIO_PORT}")
        if not os.path.isdir(SPA_DIST):
            print(f"\n⚠️  {SPA_BUILD_HINT}")
        print("\nPress Ctrl+C to stop both.\n")

        # Wait for either process to exit unexpectedly
        while True:
            rc_server = server.poll()
            rc_studio = studio.poll()

            if rc_server is not None:
                print(f"\nServer exited unexpectedly (code {rc_server}).")
                break

            if rc_studio is not None:

                break

name: e2e-install

# Runs after the `release` workflow publishes a tag's assets: installing straight
# off the tag push raced the asset uploads and 404'd every time.
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["release"]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: "Release tag to test (e.g. v0.3.0)"
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  e2e-linux-macos:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve release tag
        id: tag
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DISPATCH_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
          RUN_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          tag="${DISPATCH_TAG:-$RUN_BRANCH}"
          if ! gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            tag="$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name)"
          fi
          case "$tag" in
            v*) ;;
            *) echo "::error::Could not resolve a release tag (got '$tag')"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Testing $tag"
      - name: Install
        env:
          TAG: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/releases/download/$TAG/install.sh" \
            | AGENTIC_ODI_INSTALL_DIR="$RUNNER_TEMP/odi-home" AGENTIC_ODI_BIN_DIR="$RUNNER_TEMP/odi-bin" bash
      - name: Smoke test
        run: |
          export PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/odi-bin:$PATH"
          odi --version
          odi --help
          odi outcomes score 8 2

  e2e-windows:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: windows-latest
    steps:
      - name: Resolve release tag
        id: tag
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DISPATCH_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
          RUN_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $tag = $env:DISPATCH_TAG
          if (-not $tag) { $tag = $env:RUN_BRANCH }
          gh api "repos/$env:GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/tags/$tag" *> $null
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            $tag = gh api "repos/$env:GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name
          }
          if ($tag -notmatch '^v') { throw "Could not resolve a release tag (got '$tag')" }
          "tag=$tag" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_OUTPUT -Append -Encoding utf8
          Write-Output "Testing $tag"
      - name: Install
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          TAG: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          $url = "https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/releases/download/$env:TAG/install.ps1"
          $env:AGENTIC_ODI_INSTALL_DIR = "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\odi-home"
          $env:AGENTIC_ODI_BIN_DIR = "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\odi-bin"
          irm $url | iex
      - name: Smoke test
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $env:PATH = "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\odi-bin;$env:PATH"
          odi --version
          odi --help

name: release-please

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

# Releases are meant to complete without a human in the loop:
#   1. release-please opens/updates the release PR
#   2. this workflow arms auto-merge on it (the repo requires the `CI green`
#      status check on main, so it merges only once CI is green)
#   3. the merge is pushed by the GitHub App below, which is what makes the
#      push trigger this workflow again, cut the tag, and start the asset
#      builds. GITHUB_TOKEN-authored pushes and merges trigger nothing, which
#      is why releases used to need a maintainer.
permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  release-please:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check for GitHub App credentials
        id: app-check
        env:
          APP_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$APP_CLIENT_ID" ] && [ -n "$APP_PRIVATE_KEY" ]; then
            echo "configured=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "configured=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::warning title=Release automation is degraded::RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID and/or RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY are missing, so release-please falls back to GITHUB_TOKEN. GitHub holds workflow runs created from GITHUB_TOKEN-authored pushes (\"This workflow requires approval from a maintainer\") and ignores the tag it creates, so this release needs a maintainer approval and ships without binaries. See 'Release automation' in README.md."
          fi

      - name: Create GitHub App token
        id: app-token
        if: steps.app-check.outputs.configured == 'true'
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
        with:
          client-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          permission-contents: write
          permission-issues: write
          permission-pull-requests: write

      - name: Release Please
        id: release
        uses: googleapis/release-please-action@v4
        with:
          config-file: release-please-config.json
          manifest-file: .release-please-manifest.json
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Arm auto-merge on the release PR
        id: auto-merge
        if: steps.release.outputs.prs_created == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
          PRS: ${{ steps.release.outputs.prs }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for pr in $(echo "$PRS" | jq -r '.[].number'); do
            state="$(gh pr view "$pr" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state --jq .state)"
            if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
              echo "Skipping #$pr (state: $state)"
              continue
            fi
            echo "Arming auto-merge on #$pr"
            gh pr merge --auto --squash "$pr" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          done

name: e2e-install

# Runs after the `release` workflow publishes a tag's assets: installing straight
# off the tag push raced the asset uploads and 404'd every time.
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["release"]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: "Release tag to test (e.g. v0.3.0)"
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  e2e-linux-macos:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve release tag
        id: tag
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DISPATCH_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
          RUN_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          tag="${DISPATCH_TAG:-$RUN_BRANCH}"
          if ! gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            tag="$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name)"
          fi
          case "$tag" in
            v*) ;;
            *) echo "::error::Could not resolve a release tag (got '$tag')"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Testing $tag"
      - name: Install
        env:
          TAG: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/releases/download/$TAG/install.sh" \
            | AGENTIC_ODI_INSTALL_DIR="$RUNNER_TEMP/odi-home" AGENTIC_ODI_BIN_DIR="$RUNNER_TEMP/odi-bin" bash
      - name: Smoke test
        run: |
          export PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/odi-bin:$PATH"
          odi --version
          odi --help
          odi outcomes score 8 2

  e2e-windows:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: windows-latest
    steps:
      - name: Resolve release tag
        id: tag
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DISPATCH_TAG: ${{ inputs.tag }}
          RUN_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $tag = $env:DISPATCH_TAG
          if (-not $tag) { $tag = $env:RUN_BRANCH }
          gh api "repos/$env:GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/tags/$tag" *> $null
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            $tag = gh api "repos/$env:GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name
          }
          if ($tag -notmatch '^v') { throw "Could not resolve a release tag (got '$tag')" }
          "tag=$tag" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_OUTPUT -Append -Encoding utf8
          Write-Output "Testing $tag"
      - name: Install
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          TAG: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          $url = "https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/releases/download/$env:TAG/install.ps1"
          $env:AGENTIC_ODI_INSTALL_DIR = "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\odi-home"
          $env:AGENTIC_ODI_BIN_DIR = "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\odi-bin"
          irm $url | iex
      - name: Smoke test
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $env:PATH = "$env:RUNNER_TEMP\odi-bin;$env:PATH"
          odi --version
          odi --help
          odi outcomes score 8 2

name: release-please

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

# Releases are meant to complete without a human in the loop:
#   1. release-please opens/updates the release PR
#   2. this workflow arms auto-merge on it (the repo requires the `CI green`
#      status check on main, so it merges only once CI is green)
#   3. the merge is pushed by the GitHub App below, which is what makes the
#      push trigger this workflow again, cut the tag, and start the asset
#      builds. GITHUB_TOKEN-authored pushes and merges trigger nothing, which
#      is why releases used to need a maintainer.
permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  release-please:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check for GitHub App credentials
        id: app-check
        env:
          APP_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          APP_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$APP_CLIENT_ID" ] && [ -n "$APP_PRIVATE_KEY" ]; then
            echo "configured=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "configured=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::warning title=Release automation is degraded::RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID and/or RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY are missing, so release-please falls back to GITHUB_TOKEN. GitHub holds workflow runs created from GITHUB_TOKEN-authored pushes (\"This workflow requires approval from a maintainer\") and ignores the tag it creates, so this release needs a maintainer approval and ships without binaries. See 'Release automation' in README.md."
          fi

      - name: Create GitHub App token
        id: app-token
        if: steps.app-check.outputs.configured == 'true'
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v3
        with:
          client-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          permission-contents: write
          permission-issues: write
          permission-pull-requests: write

      - name: Release Please
        id: release
        uses: googleapis/release-please-action@v4
        with:
          config-file: release-please-config.json
          manifest-file: .release-please-manifest.json
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Arm auto-merge on the release PR
        id: auto-merge
        if: steps.release.outputs.prs_created == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
          PRS: ${{ steps.release.outputs.prs }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for pr in $(echo "$PRS" | jq -r '.[].number'); do
            state="$(gh pr view "$pr" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state --jq .state)"
            if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
              echo "Skipping #$pr (state: $state)"
              continue
            fi
            echo "Arming auto-merge on #$pr"
            gh pr merge --auto --squash "$pr" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          done

<skill_content name="using-git-worktrees">
# Skill: using-git-worktrees

# Using Git Worktrees

## Overview

Ensure work happens in an isolated workspace. Prefer your platform's native worktree tools. Fall back to manual git worktrees only when no native tool is available.

**Core principle:** Detect existing isolation first. Then use native tools. Then fall back to git. Never fight the harness.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace."

## Step 0: Detect Existing Isolation

**Before creating anything, check if you are already in an isolated workspace.**

```bash
GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
```

**Submodule guard:** `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON` is also true inside git submodules. Before concluding "already in a worktree," verify you are not in a submodule:

```bash
# If this returns a path, you're in a submodule, not a worktree — treat as normal repo
git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree 2>/dev/null
```

**If `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON` (and not a submodule):** You are already in a linked worktree. Skip to Step 2 (Project Setup). Do NOT create another worktree.

Report with branch state:
- On a branch: "Already in isolated workspace at `<path>` on branch `<name>`."
- Detached HEAD: "Already in isolated workspace at `<path>` (detached HEAD, externally managed). Branch creation needed at finish time."

**If `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON` (or in a submodule):** You are in a normal repo checkout.

Has the user already indicated their worktree preference in your instructions? If not, ask for consent before creating a worktree:

> "Would you like me to set up an isolated worktree? It protects your current branch from changes."

Honor any existing declared preference without asking. If the user declines consent, work in place and skip to Step 2.

## Step 1: Create Isolated Workspace

**You have two mechanisms. Try them in this order.**

### 1a. Native Worktree Tools (preferred)

The user has asked for an isolated workspace (Step 0 consent). Do you already have a way to create a worktree? It might be a tool with a name like `EnterWorktree`, `WorktreeCreate`, a `/worktree` command, or a `--worktree` flag. If you do, use it and skip to Step 2.

Native tools handle directory placement, branch creation, and cleanup automatically. Using `git worktree add` when you have a native tool creates phantom state your harness can't see or manage.

Only proceed to Step 1b if you have no native worktree tool available.

### 1b. Git Worktree Fallback

**Only use this if Step 1a does not apply** — you have no native worktree tool available. Create a worktree manually using git.

#### Directory Selection

Follow this priority order. Explicit user preference always beats observed filesystem state.

1. **Check your instructions for a declared worktree directory preference.** If the user has already specified one, use it without asking.

2. **Check for an existing project-local worktree directory:**
   ```bash
   ls -d .worktrees 2>/dev/null     # Preferred (hidden)
   ls -d worktrees 2>/dev/null      # Alternative
   ```
   If found, use it. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.

3. **If there is no other guidance available**, default to `.worktrees/` at the project root.

#### Safety Verification (project-local directories only)

**MUST verify directory is ignored before creating worktree:**

```bash
git check-ignore -q .worktrees 2>/dev/null || git check-ignore -q worktrees 2>/dev/null
```

**If NOT ignored:** Add to .gitignore, commit the change, then proceed.

**Why critical:** Prevents accidentally committing worktree contents to repository.

#### Create the Worktree

```bash
# Determine path based on chosen location
path="$LOCATION/$BRANCH_NAME"

git worktree add "$path" -b "$BRANCH_NAME"
cd "$path"
```

**Sandbox fallback:** If `git worktree add` fails with a permission error (sandbox denial), tell the user the sandbox blocked worktree creation and you're working in the current directory instead. Then run setup and baseline tests in place.

## Step 2: Project Setup

Auto-detect and run appropriate setup:

```bash
# Node.js
if [ -f package.json ]; then npm install; fi

# Rust
if [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then cargo build; fi

# Python
if [ -f requirements.txt ]; then pip install -r requirements.txt; fi
if [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then poetry install; fi

# Go
if [ -f go.mod ]; then go mod download; fi
```

## Step 3: Verify Clean Baseline

Run tests to ensure workspace starts clean:

```bash
# Use project-appropriate command
npm test / cargo test / pytest / go test ./...
```

**If tests fail:** Report failures, ask whether to proceed or investigate.

**If tests pass:** Report ready.

### Report

```
Worktree ready at <full-path>
Tests passing (<N> tests, 0 failures)
Ready to implement <feature-name>
```

## Quick Reference

| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Already in linked worktree | Skip creation (Step 0) |
| In a submodule | Treat as normal repo (Step 0 guard) |
| Native worktree tool available | Use it (Step 1a) |
| No native tool | Git worktree fallback (Step 1b) |
| `.worktrees/` exists | Use it (verify ignored) |
| `worktrees/` exists | Use it (verify ignored) |
| Both exist | Use `.worktrees/` |
| Neither exists | Check instruction file, then default `.worktrees/` |
| Directory not ignored | Add to .gitignore + commit |
| Permission error on create | Sandbox fallback, work in place |
| Tests fail during baseline | Report failures + ask |
| No package.json/Cargo.toml | Skip dependency install |

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "I'm obviously not in a worktree — no need to check" | Run Step 0. Harness-created isolation and submodules both fool eyeballing; the detection commands settle it. |
| "`git worktree add` is quicker than hunting for a native tool" | A native tool (e.g. `EnterWorktree`) owns placement, branching, and cleanup. Bypassing it is the #1 mistake — it creates phantom state your harness can't see or manage. |
| "The worktree directory is surely ignored already" | Run `git check-ignore`. An unignored worktree directory commits the whole tree into the repo. |
| "Any directory name works" | Explicit instructions beat an existing project-local directory, which beats the `.worktrees/` default. |
| "The workspace is fresh — baseline tests can wait" | A dirty baseline makes every later failure ambiguous. Run the tests now; proceeding past failures is your human partner's call. |

<skill_content name="finishing-a-development-branch">
# Skill: finishing-a-development-branch

# Finishing a Development Branch

## Overview

**Core principle:** Verify tests → Detect environment → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."

## Step 1: Verify Tests

Run the project's full test suite (`npm test` / `cargo test` / `pytest` / `go test ./...`).

**If tests fail**, report the failures and stop — the menu comes after a green suite:

```
Tests failing (<N> failures). Must fix before completing:

[Show failures]
```

**If tests pass:** continue to Step 2.

## Step 2: Detect Environment

```bash
GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
# Capture now, while still inside the workspace — Step 5 changes directory
# before cleanup (Step 6) needs this value
WORKTREE_PATH=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
```

This determines which menu to show and how cleanup works:

| State | Menu | Cleanup |
|-------|------|---------|
| `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON` (normal repo) | Standard 3 options | No worktree to clean up |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, named branch | Standard 3 options | Provenance-based (see Step 6) |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, detached HEAD | Reduced 2 options (no merge) | Externally managed — leave in place |

## Step 3: Determine Base Branch

The base branch is whatever this work forked from — usually named in the
plan, the conversation, or the branch's upstream. If it is not already
known, ask: "This branch split from <your best guess> - is that correct?"
Confirm before merging: merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo.

## Step 4: Present Options

**Normal repo and named-branch worktree — present exactly these 3 options:**

```
Implementation complete. What would you like to do?

1. Merge back to <base-branch> locally
2. Push and create a Pull Request
3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

**Detached HEAD — present exactly these 2 options:**

```
Implementation complete. You're on a detached HEAD (externally managed workspace).

1. Push as new branch and create a Pull Request
2. Keep as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

Present the menu exactly as written — concise, with every option coming
from the list above. Discarding the work happens only in response to your
human partner explicitly asking for it (see "If your human partner asks to
discard the work" below). Wait for their answer; the integration decision
is theirs.

## Step 5: Execute Choice

### Option 1: Merge Locally

```bash
# Get main repo root for CWD safety
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"

# Merge first — verify success before removing anything
git checkout <base-branch>
git pull
git merge <feature-branch>

# Verify tests on merged result
<test command>
```

If tests fail on the merged result: stop, leave the worktree and branch in
place, and investigate — nothing has been pushed, so the merge is local
and recoverable.

Once the merged result is green: clean up the worktree (Step 6), then
delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -d <feature-branch>
```

### Option 2: Push and Create PR

```bash
git push -u origin <feature-branch>
# From a detached HEAD, name the new branch on the remote:
# git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch>
```

Then create the pull/merge request against <base-branch> with the forge's
tooling — its CLI if one is available, or the creation URL most forges
print when you push — following the repo's PR template and conventions if
present, and report the URL to your human partner.

Keep the worktree — your human partner iterates on PR feedback there.

### Option 3: Keep As-Is

Report: "Keeping branch <name>. Worktree preserved at <path>."

### If your human partner asks to discard the work

This path exists only as a response to an explicit request to throw the
work away. Confirm first:

```
This will permanently delete:
- Branch <name>
- All commits: <commit-list>
- Worktree at <path>

Type 'discard' to confirm.
```

Wait for that exact confirmation. When it arrives:

```bash
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"
```

Then clean up the worktree (Step 6) and force-delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -D <feature-branch>
```

## Step 6: Cleanup Workspace

**Runs for Option 1 and confirmed discards.** Options 2 and 3 always
preserve the worktree. Both callers have already changed directory to the
main repo root — worktree removal must run from outside the worktree —
and use the `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_COMMON`/`WORKTREE_PATH` values captured in
Step 2, from before that directory change.

**If `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON`:** Normal repo, no worktree to clean up. Done.

**If `WORKTREE_PATH` is under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`:** Superpowers
created this worktree — we own cleanup:

```bash
git worktree remove "$WORKTREE_PATH"
git worktree prune  # Self-healing: clean up any stale registrations
```

**If removal is refused** (`contains modified or untracked files`): the
worktree holds files that exist nowhere else — uncommitted plans, notes,
or scratch work. Never `--force` on your own initiative. Show your human
partner what is at stake and ask:

```bash
git -C "$WORKTREE_PATH" status --porcelain -uall
```

```
Worktree removal refused — these files were never committed:

<file list>

1. Commit them to <branch> before cleanup
2. Move them into <main repo root>
3. Delete them (unrecoverable)

Which?
```

Carry out the choice, then remove the worktree.

**Otherwise:** The host environment owns this workspace — leave it in
place. If your platform provides a workspace-exit tool, use it.

## Quick Reference

| Option | Merge | Push | Keep Worktree | Cleanup Branch |
|--------|-------|------|---------------|----------------|
| 1. Merge locally | yes | - | - | yes |
| 2. Create PR | - | yes | yes | - |
| 3. Keep as-is | - | - | yes | - |
| Discard (explicit request only) | - | - | - | yes (force) |

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Tests passed earlier this session" | Run the suite on the tree you are about to integrate. A green run only proves the tree it ran on. |
| "They obviously want it merged" | Integration is your human partner's decision. Present the menu and wait. |
| "They seem done with this feature — I'll offer to discard it" | The menu is complete as written. Discard happens only when your human partner asks for it in so many words. |
| "'Yeah, get rid of it' counts as confirmation" | Only the typed word `discard` authorizes deletion. |
| "The PR is up, so the worktree is clutter now" | PR feedback gets fixed in that worktree. It stays until the work lands. |
| "This other worktree looks stale — I'll clean it too" | Clean up only worktrees under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`. Everything else belongs to the host. |
| "Removal refused — `--force` is just finishing the cleanup" | The refusal means files exist only in that worktree. `--force` destroys them permanently. Show your human partner and ask. |
| "The merged-result failure is probably flaky" | A failing merged result stops everything. Branch and worktree stay put while you investigate. |
| "The base branch is obviously main" | Confirm the fork point or ask. Merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo. |
| "The push was rejected — force-push will fix it" | A rejected push means the remote moved. Investigate; force-push only on your human partner's explicit request. |

This page changes when the code does. ## Code Overview A [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) with shared tooling at the root. For the desktop app, use `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev`. See [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). +The Studio opens as a conversation: describe a job or a customer frustration, or +use the left drawer to open the opportunity landscape, job map, impact +simulation, evidence, and capture panels beside the chat. + The Studio needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support to drive its agent — see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md). ### CLI at a glance The CLI is local-first, so data commands work without a running server: ```bash python -m agentic_odi_cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m agentic_odi_cli --help # show available options and commands python -m agentic_odi_cli # start interactive chat in a terminal agentic-odi jobs list # Jobs-to-be-Done agentic-odi steps list --job-id agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id agentic-odi customer-outcomes list agentic-odi evidence list --job-id agentic-odi schema # canonical JSON schema for every entity agentic-odi score 8 2 # ODI opportunity score → 14.00 ``` Add `--backend mcp` to route data commands through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`).  # Running The Living Studio
 
 **The Living Studio** is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation:
 an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact
 Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent
 connected to the MCP server.
 
 The Studio runs three ways. All of them serve the same SPA, which talks only to
 the sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:8100` — the SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM
 directly.
 
 ## Architecture
 
 ```text
 ┌────────────────────────────┐  /api (JSON)  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
 │  Living Studio SPA         │ ────────────▶ │  apps/studio-api (sidecar)    │
 │  React + TS + Vite         │  /api/chat    │  FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100    │
 │  (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │  - config / health / canvas   │
 └────────────────────────────┘  SSE stream   │  - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │
                                              │  - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop)  │
                                              └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                              │ MCP (HTTP)
                                                              ▼
                                              ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                              │  apps/mcp-server :8000/mcp    │
                                              └───────────────────────────────┘
                                                              ▲
                                                              │ OpenAI-compatible
                                              ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                                              │  Your local LLM backend       │
                                              └───────────────────────────────┘
 ```
 
+## Interface
+
+The Studio opens as a conversation, not a dashboard.
+
+| Surface | What it does |
+|---|---|
+| **Hero** | One rotating headline above the composer: a greeting (time of day, plus your name if you set one in Settings), what is already on the canvas, or what the studio can do. It cycles every few seconds and stays still under `prefers-reduced-motion`. |
+| **Suggestion pills** | Below the headline. Some open a workspace panel (landscape, simulate, capture), others start a conversation. They change as the canvas fills up. |
+| **Composer** | Docked at the bottom of the transcript. `Enter` sends, `Shift`+`Enter` adds a line, `Cmd/Ctrl`+`K` focuses it, and the send button becomes a stop button while a reply streams. |
+| **Drawer** (left) | New conversation, the five workspace panels, live model/MCP status, and Settings. Collapses to an icon rail with `Cmd/Ctrl`+`B`; becomes an overlay sheet on narrow screens. |
+| **Workspace panel** (right) | The classic UI — opportunity landscape, job map, impact simulation, evidence, direct capture, settings — opens beside the conversation, never on top of it. |
+
+Replies render Markdown (headings, lists, emphasis, inline and fenced code).
+Tool calls appear inline as small trace chips while the agent works.
+
 ## 1. Web — production build (recommended for a quick look)
 
 ```bash
 npm --prefix apps/studio run build   # build the SPA into apps/studio/dist
 python scripts/dev.py            # starts MCP :8000 + sidecar :8100
 ```
 
 | Service | URL |
 |---|---|
 | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp |
 | Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 |
 
 `python scripts/dev.py` starts both processes concurrently; press **Ctrl+C** to
 stop both.
 
 ## 2. Web — dev with hot reload
 
 Vite proxies `/api` to the sidecar:
 
 ```bash
 npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full   # MCP + sidecar + Vite together
 # open http://localhost:5173
 ```
 
 ## 3. Desktop — Tauri 2
 
 The app spawns the MCP server and sidecar itself:
 
 ```bash
 npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev     # dev window
 npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri build   # bundles: .deb / .AppImage (Linux), .app / .dmg (macOS), .msi / .exe (Windows)
 ```
 
 > [!NOTE]
 > **Tauri prerequisites.** The desktop build needs the WebKitGTK toolchain and
 > Rust 1.90+. On Debian/Ubuntu:
 >
 > ```bash
 > sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential pkg-config curl wget file \
 >   libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf xdg-utils libfuse2t64
 > ```
 >
 > The Tauri CLI ships as the `@tauri-apps/cli` npm dev dependency
 > (`npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri`). The sidecar is launched with
 > `uv run python -m …` from the repository root; if the app cannot locate the
 > repo root, set `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT`.
 
 ## Desktop signing & updater secrets
 
 Self-updating and code signing are **env-driven**: if a secret is absent, an
 unsigned artifact is produced instead of failing. CI reads these from GitHub
 Actions secrets.
 
 | Secret | Purpose |
 |---|---|
 | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` | Signs updater artifacts (`.sig`) and the `latest.json` manifest. A tagged release fails loudly without it. Generate with `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate`. |
 | `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` | Password for the private key (optional when the key has none). |
 | `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` / `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | macOS Developer ID certificate (base64 `.p12`) and its password. |
 | `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` | macOS signing identity. |
 | `APPLE_ID` / `APPLE_PASSWORD` / `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | macOS notarization credentials. |
 | `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE` / `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | Windows Authenticode PFX (base64) and its password; imported by CI and injected into the bundle config. |
 
 Releases are published by `.github/workflows/tauri-release.yml` when a `v*` tag
 is pushed. The desktop app checks for updates on startup and via
 **Settings → Check for updates**.
 
 ### Managing the updater signing key
 
 The updater key pair authenticates release artifacts so an installed app can
 verify that an auto-update genuinely came from you. The **public** key is
 embedded in `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (`plugins.updater.pubkey`) and is
 safe to commit. The **private** key must never be committed, logged, printed in
 CI, or attached to a build artifact.
 
 1. **Generate a key pair** (only if you need a new one). Leave `-p ""` for a
    passwordless key, or pass a password and remember it:
 
    ```bash
    npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate -- -w ./living-studio.key -p "" -f
    ```
 
    This writes `living-studio.key` (private, `0600`) and `living-studio.key.pub`
    (public).
 
 2. **Paste the public key** into `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`:
 
    ```jsonc
    {
      "plugins": {
        "updater": {
          "endpoints": ["https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/latest.json"],
          "pubkey": "<contents of living-studio.key.pub>"
        }
      }
    }
    ```
 
 3. **Store the private key outside the repository** (the repo root is
    git-tracked; a sibling directory is not), with restricted permissions:
 
    ```bash
    mkdir -p ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys && chmod 700 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys
    mv living-studio.key ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/
    chmod 600 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
    ```
 
    Move it to a long-term secret store (password manager, 1Password/Bitwarden/
    Vault, or a private encrypted backup) when you decide where that lives.
    Losing it means future releases can no longer be signed for existing
    installs.
 
 4. **Add the private key as a GitHub Actions secret** (Settings → Secrets and
    variables → Actions → New repository secret), or via the CLI:
 
    ```bash
    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD --body ""   # only if you set a password
    ```
 
 5. **Verify** the secrets exist (values are never displayed):
 
    ```bash
    gh secret list
    ```
 
 6. **Rotate** by repeating steps 1–4, then publishing a release signed with the
    new key. Existing installs still verify against the public key compiled into
    their binary, so keep the old private key usable and publish the new public
    key ahead of the cut-over.
 
 > [!CAUTION]
 > If the private key leaks, treat auto-updates as compromised: generate a new
 > pair, rotate the Actions secret, and publish a freshly signed release.
 
 > [!IMPORTANT]
 > **Migration note.** The Streamlit UI has been removed. The Living Studio now
 > lives in `apps/studio/` (browser SPA + Tauri desktop app) and is served by the
 > `apps/studio-api` sidecar on port **8100** (previously Streamlit's `8501`).
 > Start everything with `python scripts/dev.py`. All `AGENTIC_ODI_*` environment
 > variable names, the demo dataset, and the ODI formulas are unchanged.
 
 ## Connecting an LLM
 
 The Studio needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM backend with tool-calling support to
 drive the agent. For a fully local setup, see
 [Local LLM Backend](local-llm.md).
 
 ## Agent-Driven Testing
 
 Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it starts
 both processes, opens the browser, sends a test message, and reports the results.
 
 Type `/test` to have the agent run all tests and report the results
 automatically.

input.content:
## Summary

Reorganizes the uv workspace around responsibility instead of technology. Python packages now live under `packages/`, runnable services under `apps/`, and deployment assets under `infra/`, with distribution names and import roots aligned.

## Changes

- Move `core` → `packages/core` (`agentic_odi_core`)
- Move `connectors` → `packages/connectors` (`agentic_odi_connectors`)
- Move `cli` → `apps/cli` (`agentic_odi_cli`)
- Move `mcp_server` → `apps/mcp-server` (`agentic_odi_mcp_server`)
- Move `local_server` → `apps/studio-api` (`agentic_odi_studio_api`)
- Move `studio` → `apps/studio` and `cloudflare` → `infra/cloudflare`
- Replace the `client` launcher package with `scripts/dev.py`
- Consolidate Python tooling (ruff, mypy, pytest, coverage) at the workspace root
- Update root workspace members, package metadata, PyInstaller spec, CI paths, Wrangler config, and dev/build scripts
- Add shared MCP contract tests at `tests/contract/`
- Refresh README, architecture, development, deployment, and Studio docs for the new layout

## Testing

- `uv run pytest` — 546 passed (Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12), 94% coverage
- `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` — passed
- `uv run mypy apps packages` and `uv run --directory website mypy .` — passed
- `uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages website/` — no issues
- Website tests — 34 passed
- Studio: `npm run lint`, `typecheck`, 24 Vitest tests, and production build — passed
- Cargo: `fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`, and `check` — passed
- CLI, MCP server, Studio sidecar, `scripts/dev.py`, wheel installs, PyInstaller binary, and installer e2e smoke tests — passed

## Notes

- The `agentic-odi-dev` console script is intentionally removed; use `uv run python scripts/dev.py`.
- The live MCP tool surface is unchanged (30 tools), now enforced by contract tests.
